translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouming, Pan Tiancheng, Weng Yunhuai and his younger brother Yunbiao, Yang Shixuan, and Xu Dazhong.

translations.idiomatic: Shen Renye, Wei Shude, Li Ruhui, Zheng Liben, and Li Xuetong.

translations.idiomatic: Dong Shiyuan, Li Fuxin, Dang Guohu, Yan Tingzan, and Lu Qikun and his younger brother Qipeng.

translations.idiomatic: Yu Erwang and his younger brother Erxue, Huang Hongyuan and his younger brother Fuyuan, Yan Zhonghe, and Yan Ao.

sentences.zh: 王恩榮楊獻恆任騎馬李巨勳任四

translations.literal: Wang Enrong, Yang Xianheng, Ren Qima, Li Juxun, Ren Si.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Enrong, Yang Xianheng, Ren Qima, Li Juxun, and Ren Si.

sentences.zh: 王國林藍忠=盧必升=盧必升，字寀臣，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Guolin, Lan Zhong. Lu Bisheng—Lu Bisheng, style name Caichen, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guolin and Lan Zhong. Lu Bisheng—Lu Bisheng, whose style was Caichen, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 九歲，父芳病，思得蟚蜞炙，必升挾筐求之沙上，潮至，幾死，不釋筐。

translations.literal: At nine years old, when his father Fang fell ill and longed for broiled mitten crab, Bisheng carried a basket to seek them on the sand flats; the tide came in and he nearly died, yet he would not release the basket.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nine, his father Fang fell ill and craved broiled shore crab. Bisheng took a basket to hunt for them on the tidal flats; the tide swept in and he nearly drowned, but he still would not let go of the basket.

sentences.zh: 明季遇寇，芳獨行入山，必升行求得之歸。

translations.literal: In the turmoil at the end of the Ming, when bandits came Fang went alone into the mountains; Bisheng went after him, found him, and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: In the disorders at the close of the Ming, when bandits appeared Fang went off alone into the hills. Bisheng went in search of him, found him, and led him home.

sentences.zh: 必升為叔父茂後，順治初，寇縶茂舟中，必升繞岸哭，三晝夜，不絕聲。

translations.literal: Bisheng became the heir of his uncle Mao; in the early Shunzhi reign bandits seized Mao on a boat, and Bisheng walked along the shore weeping for three days and nights without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Bisheng had been adopted as heir by his uncle Mao. Early in the Shunzhi reign bandits seized Mao aboard a boat; Bisheng paced the bank and wept for three days and nights without pause.

sentences.zh: 寇引使見茂，脅茂降，拔刃屢欲下，必升叩頭流血，乞貸死。

translations.literal: The bandits brought him to see Mao and pressed Mao to surrender; they drew their blades and repeatedly made as if to strike, while Bisheng kowtowed until his forehead bled, begging them to spare Mao's life.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits led him to Mao and tried to force Mao to submit. They drew their swords again and again as though to strike him down, while Bisheng kowtowed until blood ran from his forehead, pleading that they spare his uncle's life.

sentences.zh: 久之，寇中有義其行者，脫茂使共還。

translations.literal: After a long while, among the bandits was one who honored his conduct; he released Mao and let them return together.
translations.idiomatic: In time one of the bandits, moved by his devotion, released Mao and allowed uncle and nephew to go home together.

sentences.zh: 茂有女忌必升，嗾母遣必升往松江，使盜擊諸途。

translations.literal: Mao had a daughter who resented Bisheng; she incited her mother to send Bisheng to Songjiang and hired robbers to attack him along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Mao had a daughter who bore a grudge against Bisheng. She urged her mother to send him to Songjiang and hired men to waylay him on the journey.

sentences.zh: 盜察必升且死，曰：「爾死勿我仇，誰某實使我。

translations.literal: Seeing that Bisheng was near death, the robber said, "If you die, do not hold it against me—so-and-so is the one who really sent me."
translations.idiomatic: When the robbers saw that Bisheng was nearly dead, one said, "If you die, do not blame me—it was so-and-so who truly put me up to this."

sentences.zh: 」必昇陽死，盜擲之水，復以救免。

translations.literal: Bisheng feigned death; the robbers threw him into the water, then rescued him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Bisheng played dead. The robbers threw him into the river, but then pulled him out and he survived.

sentences.zh: 必升書告所後母，但自謝不謹被盜，所後母為感悟，為母子如初。

translations.literal: Bisheng wrote to his adoptive mother, apologizing only for his own carelessness in being robbed; his adoptive mother was moved to repentance, and mother and son were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bisheng wrote to his adoptive mother, blaming only his own carelessness for having been robbed. She was deeply moved and their bond became what it had once been.

sentences.zh: =李應麒=李應麒，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Li Yingqi—Li Yingqi was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yingqi—Li Yingqi came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 遘亂，與其父相失，被略至迤東，乞食歸。

translations.literal: When turmoil struck he was separated from his father, was carried off to eastern Yunnan, and returned home begging for food.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of war he lost his father, was taken captive to the far east of the province, and made his way home by begging along the road.

sentences.zh: 喪母，勸父再娶，後母至，遇應麒虐，應麒賣卜以養。

translations.literal: After his mother died he urged his father to remarry; when his stepmother came she treated Yingqi harshly, and he supported the household by selling divinations.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he persuaded his father to marry again. His stepmother was cruel to him, yet he supported the family by telling fortunes in the streets.

sentences.zh: 失後母意，輒笞楚，跪而受杖。

translations.literal: Whenever he displeased his stepmother she would beat him with the stick, and he would kneel and accept the blows.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he fell short of her wishes she would thrash him, and he would kneel and take the beating without protest.

sentences.zh: 後乃被逐，事父母愈謹。

translations.literal: Later he was driven out, yet he served his parents all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually turned out of the house, yet he attended to both parents with even greater devotion.

sentences.zh: 父生日，賣卜得雞米，持歸為壽。

translations.literal: On his father's birthday he earned a chicken and rice from divination and brought them home as a birthday gift.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's birthday he earned enough from fortune-telling to buy a chicken and rice, which he carried home as a gift.

sentences.zh: 佃人田，方耕，聞後母病，輟耕走三十里求醫藥。

translations.literal: While tenant-farming, he was in the middle of plowing when he heard his stepmother was ill; he stopped work and ran thirty li to fetch medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He was plowing rented fields when word came that his stepmother was ill. He left the plow and ran thirty li to find a physician and medicine.

sentences.zh: 後母生三子，友愛無間。

translations.literal: His stepmother bore three sons, and he was on affectionate terms with them without break.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother bore three sons, and he loved them as his own brothers without the slightest estrangement.

sentences.zh: 後母久乃悟，卒善視焉。

translations.literal: After a long while his stepmother came to her senses and in the end treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: In time his stepmother understood his heart and at last treated him with kindness.

sentences.zh: =李中德=李中德，漢​​軍旗人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongde—Li Zhongde was a Han Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongde—Li Zhongde belonged to the Han military banners.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，父從征福建，中德亦出參陝西軍事，奉母以行。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign his father campaigned in Fujian; Zhongde also went out to take part in military affairs in Shaanxi, bringing his mother with him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign his father marched on Fujian while Zhongde himself served in the Shaanxi theater, taking his mother with him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 事畢，還京師，父先自福建還，已娶妾生子矣。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished they returned to the capital; his father had already come back from Fujian and had taken a concubine who bore him a son.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaigns ended they returned to Beijing. His father had come back from Fujian ahead of them and had already taken a concubine who had borne him a son.

sentences.zh: 中德母至，父暱妾而出嫡，拒不相見。

translations.literal: When Zhongde's mother arrived, his father favored the concubine and cast out the legitimate wife, refusing to see her.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongde's mother arrived, his father doted on the concubine and turned his lawful wife out of the house, refusing even to meet her.

sentences.zh: 中德為請，叩頭流血，父終不聽。

translations.literal: Zhongde pleaded on her behalf, kowtowing until his forehead bled, but his father would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde begged for her, kowtowing until blood streamed from his forehead, yet his father would not relent.

sentences.zh: 請得居別室，亦不聽，及營室東直門外奉母，早晚侍父側無幾微憾，善視諸庶弟。

translations.literal: He asked that she be allowed to live in a separate room, but that too was refused; he then built a house outside Dongzhimen Gate to support his mother, yet morning and evening he attended his father's side without the slightest resentment and treated all his younger half-brothers kindly.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that his mother be housed separately, but his father refused even that. Zhongde built a dwelling outside Dongzhimen to support her, yet still attended his father morning and evening without a trace of bitterness and treated his half-brothers with affection.

sentences.zh: 越六年，父病棘，乃告父迎母還，父深悔焉，旋卒，妾亦死。

translations.literal: After six years his father fell gravely ill; Zhongde then urged his father to welcome his mother back, and his father deeply repented; soon after he died, and the concubine died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later, when his father lay critically ill, Zhongde persuaded him to bring his mother home. His father was filled with remorse, but died soon after, and the concubine died as well.

sentences.zh: 中德母撫妾生四子如己出，中德亦友愛如父在時。

translations.literal: Zhongde's mother reared the four sons born to the concubine as if they were her own, and Zhongde likewise showed brotherly love as when his father was alive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde's mother raised the concubine's four sons as her own, and Zhongde continued to love them as warmly as when his father still lived.

sentences.zh: =張文齡=張文齡，字可庭，河南西華人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenling—Zhang Wenling, style name Keting, was a native of Xihua in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenling—Zhang Wenling, whose style was Keting, came from Xihua in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父暱妾而憎其母，文齡事父撫庶弟甚篤，庶弟亦感之，而父終不悟，逐文齡。

translations.literal: His father favored a concubine and hated Wenling's mother; Wenling served his father and reared his younger half-brothers with great devotion, and the half-brothers were moved as well, yet his father never came to his senses and drove Wenling out.
translations.idiomatic: His father doted on a concubine and despised Wenling's mother. Wenling served his father faithfully and cared tenderly for his half-brothers, who were deeply moved in turn, but his father never understood and cast Wenling out.

sentences.zh: 文齡號泣呼天自懲艾，謂不復比於人，未嘗一言揚親過。

translations.literal: Wenling wailed to heaven and punished himself, saying he was no longer fit to rank among men, and never once spoke of his parent's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Wenling wept to heaven and blamed himself alone, declaring that he was unworthy to stand among other men, and he never once spoke ill of his father.

sentences.zh: 遠近慕其行，遣子弟從遊，得束脩，因庶弟以獻其父，或不得通，循牆走，泣且望，見者皆泣下。

translations.literal: Near and far admired his conduct and sent their sons and younger brothers to study with him; he received tuition and, through his half-brothers, offered it to his father; sometimes he could not gain access, and would walk along the wall weeping and gazing up—those who saw it all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: People far and near admired his character and sent their sons to study under him. From the fees he earned he sent gifts to his father by way of his half-brothers. When he was refused entry he would pace along the wall, weeping as he looked toward the house, and all who saw him wept as well.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，成進士，父榮之，意稍改。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he passed the metropolitan examination; his father took pride in it and his attitude softened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign he passed the metropolitan examination. His father was proud of him and his heart began to change.

sentences.zh: 八年，就吏部選，京師地震，死者眾，文齡亦與焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went to the Ministry of Personnel for appointment; an earthquake struck the capital and many died, Wenling among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he went to Beijing for appointment through the Ministry of Personnel. An earthquake struck the capital, killing many, and Wenling was among the dead.

sentences.zh: 鄒一桂與為友，歸其喪，父始悟其孝，為之慟。

translations.literal: Zou Yigui was his friend and brought back his coffin; only then did his father realize his filial devotion and grieved for him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Zou Yigui brought his body home. Only then did his father grasp how filial he had been, and he mourned him with overwhelming grief.

sentences.zh: =黎安理=黎安理，貴州遵義人。

translations.literal: Li Anli—Li Anli was a native of Zunyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anli—Li Anli came from Zunyi in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖母卒，复娶而悍，父不容於後母，客授四川灌縣，遂卒，葬焉。

translations.literal: After his grandmother died his grandfather remarried, and the new wife was fierce; his father could not remain in the household of his stepmother, went out as a tutor to Guan County in Sichuan, died there, and was buried there.
translations.idiomatic: After his grandmother died his grandfather took another wife, a harsh woman. His father could not endure life with his stepmother, went to Guan County in Sichuan as a private tutor, died there, and was buried there.

sentences.zh: 母還母家，安理方十歲，留祖父母所。

translations.literal: His mother returned to her parents' home; Anli was only ten and remained with his grandparents.
translations.idiomatic: His mother went back to her own family. Anli was only ten and was left in the care of his grandparents.

sentences.zh: 祖母遇之虐，晝則令刈薪，夜督舂，舂重不舉，繩絡碓，以足挽之。

translations.literal: His grandmother treated him cruelly: by day she made him cut firewood, by night she forced him to pound grain; when the pestle was too heavy to lift he tied a rope to the mortar and pulled it with his foot.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother abused him cruelly. By day she set him to cut firewood; by night she made him pound grain. When the pestle was too heavy for his arms he lashed a rope to the mortar and worked it with his foot.

sentences.zh: 恆不使得飽。

translations.literal: She constantly kept him from eating his fill.
translations.idiomatic: She never let him eat enough to be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 嘗取毒蠚納其口。

translations.literal: Once she took a poisonous wasp and put it in his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Once she thrust a venomous wasp into his mouth.

sentences.zh: 誘之溪側，推墮水。

translations.literal: She lured him to the stream bank and pushed him into the water.
translations.idiomatic: She lured him to the bank of a stream and pushed him in.

sentences.zh: 皆瀕死，遇救蘇。

translations.literal: Each time he was near death but was rescued and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he was at the point of death, yet someone saved him and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 既長，習舉子業，出客授佐家。

translations.literal: When he had grown up he studied for the examinations and went out as a tutor to help support the family.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older he prepared for the civil examinations and went out teaching to help support the household.

sentences.zh: 祖父卒，為治喪葬。

translations.literal: When his grandfather died he arranged the funeral and burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandfather died he saw to the funeral and burial himself.

sentences.zh: 祖母病，侍疾不倦，卒，又為治喪葬，無缺禮。

translations.literal: When his grandmother fell ill he nursed her tirelessly; when she died he again arranged funeral and burial without omitting any rite.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother fell ill he nursed her without rest. After she died he again conducted her funeral and burial, omitting no proper observance.

sentences.zh: 其事祖父母凡三十有四年。

translations.literal: He served his grandparents for thirty-four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He had served his grandparents for thirty-four years in all.

sentences.zh: 痛父客死，恆詣灌縣謁墓。

translations.literal: Grieving that his father had died far from home, he regularly went to Guan County to visit the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that his father had died abroad, he made regular pilgrimages to Guan County to tend the grave.

sentences.zh: 母復歸，事之孝。

translations.literal: When his mother returned he served her filially.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother came home again he cared for her with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 兩弟不勝祖母虐，出走，安理往來黔、蜀，求得仲弟還。

translations.literal: His two younger brothers could not endure their grandmother's cruelty and ran away; Anli traveled back and forth between Guizhou and Sichuan until he found his second brother and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: His two younger brothers, unable to bear their grandmother's abuse, fled. Anli traveled between Guizhou and Sichuan until he found his second brother and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 季弟客死，撫其孤。

translations.literal: His youngest brother died abroad, and he reared the orphan left behind.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother died far from home, and he raised the orphan child left behind.

sentences.zh: 安理晚舉乾隆四十四年鄉試，授永清教諭，遷山東長山知縣，有治績。

translations.literal: Anli passed the provincial examination late, in the forty-fourth year of Qianlong; he was appointed instructor at Yongqing, then transferred to be magistrate of Changshan in Shandong, where he achieved good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Anli passed the provincial examinations only late in life, in the forty-fourth year of Qianlong. He was appointed director of studies at Yongqing and later became magistrate of Changshan in Shandong, where he earned a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 告歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He requested leave to retire and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: =易良德=易良德，湖南黔陽人。

translations.literal: Yi Liangde—Yi Liangde was a native of Qianyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liangde—Yi Liangde came from Qianyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 出為世父志宰後。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption as heir to his father's elder brother Zhizai.
translations.idiomatic: He had been adopted as heir by his father's elder brother Zhizai.

sentences.zh: 志宰性急，屢撫兄弟子，皆不相能，遣還本支。

translations.literal: Zhizai was quick-tempered; he repeatedly took nephews as heirs, but none could get along with him, and he sent them back to their own branches.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizai had a quick temper. He had taken several nephews as heirs in turn, but none could live with him, and he sent each back to his own branch of the family.

sentences.zh: 最後得良德，良德能先意承志，得其歡心。

translations.literal: At last he obtained Liangde, who could anticipate his wishes and win his affection.
translations.idiomatic: At last he took Liangde, who could read his wishes in advance and truly won his heart.

sentences.zh: 有疾，晝夜侍，寢食俱廢，里人無子者恆舉良德相慰藉。

translations.literal: When Zhizai fell ill Liangde attended him day and night, neglecting sleep and food; childless men in the village would always cite Liangde to comfort one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhizai fell ill Liangde nursed him day and night, forgetting sleep and meals. Childless neighbors would point to Liangde to console one another.

sentences.zh: 方立禮，江蘇江都人。

translations.literal: Fang Lili was a native of Jiangdu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Lili came from Jiangdu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 母歾，後母遇之虐，怒輒與大杖，立禮謹受無懟。

translations.literal: After his mother died his stepmother treated him harshly; in anger she would beat him with a heavy staff, and Lili accepted it respectfully without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died his stepmother abused him. In anger she would thrash him with a heavy stick, and Lili bore it meekly without a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 一日，杖幾絕，及蘇，無變容。

translations.literal: One day the beating nearly killed him; when he revived his expression was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: One day a beating nearly killed him. When he came to, his face showed no change at all.

sentences.zh: 父歾，遂逐立禮。

translations.literal: When his father died they drove Lili out.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died they cast Lili out of the house.

sentences.zh: 立禮時時候門外問起居，疾則憂懼不食，愈乃已。

translations.literal: Lili would constantly wait outside the gate to inquire after his stepmother's health; when she fell ill he would worry and refuse to eat until she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Lili would wait outside the gate to ask after her health. When she fell ill he would fret and go without food until she was well again.

sentences.zh: 妻洪，亦孝謹，日受鞭撻，後母稍自悔，為少戢。

translations.literal: His wife Hong was also filial and careful; she too was whipped daily, until his stepmother gradually repented and restrained herself somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Hong was equally dutiful and careful, and she too was beaten every day. In time his stepmother felt remorse and eased off somewhat.

sentences.zh: 後母勿，為之哀毀。

translations.literal: When his stepmother died he mourned her with grief that wasted his body.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died he mourned her with such grief that his health was broken.

sentences.zh: 後母二子皆早死，立禮育其子女如己出。

translations.literal: His stepmother's two sons had both died young, and Lili reared their children as his own.
translations.idiomatic: Both of his stepmother's sons had died young, and Lili raised their children as if they were his own.

sentences.zh: 丁世忠，湖南黔陽人。

translations.literal: Ding Shizhong was a native of Qianyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shizhong came from Qianyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 母初未有子，父娶妾，母生世忠。

translations.literal: At first his mother had no son; his father took a concubine, and then his mother bore Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: At first his mother had borne no son, so his father took a concubine. Soon afterward his mother gave birth to Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 妾亦有子女而悍，惡世忠，嘗酖之，不死。

translations.literal: The concubine also had children and was fierce; she hated Shizhong and once poisoned him, but he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine too had children and was fierce. She hated Shizhong and once poisoned him, but he survived.

sentences.zh: 父懦，令別室居，世忠事兩母無懟。

translations.literal: His father was weak and had him live in a separate room, yet Shizhong served both mothers without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His father was timid and made him live apart, yet Shizhong served both mothers without the slightest complaint.

sentences.zh: 庶弟無禮於世忠，嫡母喪，不欲持服，世忠皆不與較。

translations.literal: His younger half-brother was disrespectful toward Shizhong; when their mother by the first wife died the half-brother did not wish to wear mourning, yet Shizhong never quarreled with him over it.
translations.idiomatic: His half-brother treated him rudely. When their lawful mother died the half-brother refused to wear mourning, yet Shizhong never held it against him.

sentences.zh: 庶弟坐事破家，世忠亦中落，仍割田畀之。

translations.literal: His half-brother was ruined by involvement in a legal case; Shizhong's own fortunes also declined, yet he still divided fields and gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: His half-brother was ruined by a lawsuit. Shizhong's own family fortunes had fallen as well, yet he still carved out part of his land and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 汪良緒，江蘇吳江人。

translations.literal: Wang Liangxu was a native of Wujiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liangxu came from Wujiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父嗜博，母諫，忤父，為父逐。

translations.literal: His father was addicted to gambling; his mother remonstrated with him, offended his father, and was driven out by him.
translations.idiomatic: His father was addicted to gambling. When his mother remonstrated with him she angered her husband, who turned her out of the house.

sentences.zh: 良緒日夜號泣，求返其母。

translations.literal: Liangxu wept day and night, begging that his mother be allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Liangxu wept day and night, pleading that his mother be brought back.

sentences.zh: 父怒，並逐之，乃奉母依其妻父居。

translations.literal: His father in anger drove him out as well; he then supported his mother while living with his wife's father.
translations.idiomatic: His father in anger cast him out too. He took his mother to live with his father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 父以博破家，亦來與共居，母出奩貲易田，盡為父所鬻，良緒客授以養。

translations.literal: His father ruined the family through gambling and also came to live with them; his mother used her dowry to buy fields, and his father sold them all; Liangxu supported the household by teaching as a tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His father gambled away the family fortune and came to live with them as well. His mother used her dowry to buy land, but his father sold every field. Liangxu supported them by teaching abroad.

sentences.zh: 方暑，父撤床上帳償博進，屢易屢鬻，良緒亦不具帳。

translations.literal: In the heat of summer his father took down the bed curtains to pay gambling debts; they were replaced again and again and sold again and again, and Liangxu too went without curtains.
translations.idiomatic: One summer his father stripped the bed curtains to settle gambling debts. Curtains were replaced and sold over and over, and Liangxu went without any himself.

sentences.zh: 晨起，蚊跡遍其體。

translations.literal: When he rose in the morning mosquito bites covered his whole body.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke in the morning his whole body was covered with mosquito bites.

sentences.zh: 母多病，良緒必親視湯藥。

translations.literal: His mother was often ill, and Liangxu always personally prepared her medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was often ill, and Liangxu always prepared her medicine himself.

sentences.zh: 出客授，母疾病，方冬，水凍舟阻，履冰而還。

translations.literal: While teaching away from home he heard his mother was ill; it was deep winter, the water was frozen and boats could not pass, yet he walked across the ice to return.
translations.idiomatic: He was teaching away from home when he learned his mother was ill. It was midwinter, the rivers were frozen and boats could not run, yet he walked across the ice to reach her.

sentences.zh: 母既歾，哭泣無常，寢

translations.literal: After his mother died he wept without restraint and in sleep
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he wept without restraint. In bed he

sentences.zh: 不解絰，稍寐輒呼阿母，寤則大慟，未終喪而卒。

translations.literal: never removed his mourning headband; whenever he dozed he would cry for his mother, and when he woke he would wail greatly; before the mourning period had ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: never took off his mourning headband. Whenever he dozed he would cry for his mother, and when he woke he would wail bitterly. Before the mourning period had ended, he died.

sentences.zh: 卒後視其枕，麻布包土★M6也。

translations.literal: After his death they looked at his pillow—it was nothing but earth wrapped in hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: After his death they looked at his pillow: it was nothing but earth wrapped in hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 賈錫成，江蘇宜興人。

translations.literal: Jia Xicheng was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xicheng came from Yixing in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父映乾，性嚴。

translations.literal: His father Yingqian was stern by nature.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingqian was stern by nature.

sentences.zh: 錫成生而生母吳以小過逢映乾怒，遂去不返。

translations.literal: When Xicheng was born his birth mother Wu, on account of a small fault, provoked Yingqian's anger and left, never to return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Xicheng was born his birth mother Wu offended Yingqian over a trifling matter. She left and never came back.

sentences.zh: 錫成稍長，鄰兒嘲無母，問得其故，悲不勝。

translations.literal: When Xicheng had grown a little, neighborhood boys mocked him for having no mother; he asked the reason and was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: As Xicheng grew older, neighborhood boys taunted him for having no mother. When he learned why, grief overwhelmed him.

sentences.zh: 甫成童，屢出訪母。

translations.literal: As soon as he reached boyhood he went out again and again to seek his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he come of age when he set out repeatedly to find his mother.

sentences.zh: 過無錫，夢至尼菴，嫗予食，甚慈愛。

translations.literal: Passing through Wuxi, he dreamed he came to a nunnery where an old woman gave him food with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Wuxi, he dreamed of a nunnery where an old woman fed him with great tenderness.

sentences.zh: 因遍訪諸尼庵，方雪，老尼問里居，曰：「宜興。

translations.literal: He therefore visited every nunnery; it was snowing, and an old nun asked where he was from. He said, "Yixing."
translations.idiomatic: He then searched every nunnery in turn. Snow was falling. An old nun asked his home place, and he answered, "Yixing."

sentences.zh: 」因曰：「吾徒亦宜興。

translations.literal: She then said, "One of our nuns is also from Yixing."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "One of our sisters is from Yixing as well."

sentences.zh: 」入見之，即其母也。

translations.literal: He went in to see her—it was his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to see her, and it was his mother.

sentences.zh: 相持哭，母終不肯歸。

translations.literal: They embraced and wept, but his mother would not agree to return home.
translations.idiomatic: They clung to each other and wept, yet his mother still refused to go home.

sentences.zh: 錫成數省視饋食。

translations.literal: Xicheng visited her many times and brought her food.
translations.idiomatic: Xicheng visited her often and brought her provisions.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，以喪還葬，上塚哭必慟。

translations.literal: When his mother died he brought her coffin home for burial, and whenever he visited the grave he wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he brought her body home for burial. Each time he visited the grave he wept as though his heart would break.

sentences.zh: 映乾遘疫卒，錫成痛甚，伏柩側喃喃若共父語，夢中或歡笑，寤則大慟。

translations.literal: Yingqian died of plague; Xicheng was in great pain, lay beside the coffin murmuring as if talking with his father, sometimes laughed in his dreams, and when he woke would wail greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqian died of plague. Xicheng was stricken with grief. He lay beside the coffin murmuring as though speaking with his father, sometimes laughed in his sleep, and when he woke would wail bitterly.

sentences.zh: 疾作遽卒，距映乾卒才五日。

translations.literal: Illness seized him and he died suddenly, only five days after Yingqian's death.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died suddenly, only five days after his father.

sentences.zh: 王長祚，字爾昌，湖南衡陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Changzuo, style name Erchang, was a native of Hengyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Changzuo, whose style was Erchang, came from Hengyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父喬年，以富名。

translations.literal: His father Qiaonian was famed for his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiaonian was renowned for his wealth.

sentences.zh: 明季張獻忠破衡陽，喬年出避，遊騎縶長祚與次子璠求喬年所在，榜掠終不言。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, Zhang Xianzhong took Hengyang; Qiaonian fled to escape, and roaming horsemen seized Changzuo and his second son Fan, demanding to know where Qiaonian was; they beat and tortured them but in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Ming, Zhang Xianzhong captured Hengyang. Qiaonian fled, and roaming horsemen seized Changzuo and his second son Fan, demanding to know where Qiaonian was. They were beaten and tortured but would not speak.

sentences.zh: 寇挽長祚發，加刃於頸，璠號泣求代。

translations.literal: The bandits seized Changzuo by the hair and set a blade to his neck; Fan wailed and begged to die in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized Changzuo by the hair and pressed a blade to his throat. Fan wept and begged to die in his brother's stead.

sentences.zh: 寇中有騎者言：「此父子皆孝，奈何殺之？

translations.literal: Among the bandits a mounted man said, "Father and sons are all filial—how can we kill them?"
translations.idiomatic: One of the mounted bandits said, "This father and these sons are all filial. How can we kill them?"

sentences.zh: 」遂得釋。

translations.literal: They were then released.
translations.idiomatic: They were released.

sentences.zh: 劉國賓，芷江人。

translations.literal: Liu Guobin was a native of Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guobin came from Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 國初流寇入縣境，國賓負母出避，道遇寇，劫母衣，刃創國賓，血流至足。

translations.literal: In the early Qing roaming bandits entered the county; Guobin carried his mother on his back to flee, met bandits on the road, who robbed his mother of her clothes and wounded Guobin with a blade until blood ran to his feet.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty roaming bandits entered the county. Guobin carried his mother on his back to flee, met bandits on the road, who stripped his mother's clothes and slashed Guobin until blood ran to his feet.

sentences.zh: 國賓忍痛跪乞還母衣，語迫至，寇愍其孝而還之。

translations.literal: Guobin endured the pain, knelt, and begged that his mother's clothes be returned; his words were so urgent that the bandits pitied his filial devotion and gave them back.
translations.idiomatic: Guobin bore the pain, knelt, and begged for his mother's clothes. His pleas were so desperate that the bandits pitied his devotion and returned them.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，吳三桂兵至，掠族弟國宥，其母嫠也，哭之喪明。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign Wu Sangui's troops came, carried off his clansman younger brother Guoyou, whose mother was a widow; she wept until she lost her sight.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign Wu Sangui's troops came and seized his clansman Guoyou. Guoyou's mother was a widow; she wept until she went blind.

sentences.zh: 國賓行求國宥，逾年以歸，其母目復明。

translations.literal: Guobin went in search of Guoyou; after more than a year he brought him back, and his mother's eyes regained their sight.
translations.idiomatic: Guobin went in search of Guoyou. After more than a year he brought him home, and the mother's sight returned.

sentences.zh: 貧不能自存，國賓分田百畝與之。

translations.literal: Unable to support themselves in poverty, Guobin gave them a hundred mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: They were too poor to live on their own, so Guobin gave them a hundred mu of land.

sentences.zh: 曹超，安徽和州人。

translations.literal: Cao Chao was a native of Hezhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Chao came from Hezhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 順治中，鄭成功兵至，超奉父母出避，遇寇欲殺之，超號泣求代，並得免。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign Zheng Chenggong's troops came; Chao led his parents out to flee, met bandits who meant to kill them, and Chao wailed and begged to die in their place—they were all spared.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi reign Zheng Chenggong's army arrived. Chao led his parents to flee, met bandits who meant to kill them, and wailed, begging to die in their place. All were spared.

sentences.zh: 居喪，負土為墳。

translations.literal: During mourning he carried earth on his back to build the grave.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he carried earth on his back to build the grave himself.

sentences.zh: 家有紫薇，父手植也，久枯，每對之哀慟，非時復發花。

translations.literal: At home was a crape myrtle his father had planted by hand; long withered, whenever he grieved before it out of season it would bloom again.
translations.idiomatic: At home stood a crape myrtle his father had planted with his own hands. Long dead, it would bloom again out of season whenever he mourned before it.

sentences.zh: 黎興岕，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Li Xingjie was a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingjie came from Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠破長沙，略湘陰，興岕父嘉品為賊縶，將殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong took Changsha and overran Xiangyin; Xingjie's father Jiapin was seized by bandits and about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong captured Changsha and overran Xiangyin. Xingjie's father Jiapin was seized by the rebels and was about to be executed.

sentences.zh: 興岕八歲，請代父死，賊幼之，舉刀令申頸，泣曰：「此恐欺我，既殺我，复殺父，乞但殺我一人。

translations.literal: Xingjie was eight years old and asked to die in his father's place; the bandits thought him young, raised a knife and told him to stretch out his neck; weeping he said, "This is probably to deceive me—after you kill me you will kill my father again; I beg you kill only me."
translations.idiomatic: Xingjie was eight. He asked to die in his father's place. The bandits, thinking him a child, raised a knife and told him to bare his neck. Weeping, he said, "You are probably deceiving me—after you kill me you will kill my father too. I beg you kill only me."

sentences.zh: 」引頸就刀，賊兩釋之，里人稱之曰「孺孝」。

translations.literal: He stretched out his neck toward the blade; the bandits released them both, and the villagers called him "the child of filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: He stretched out his neck to the blade. The bandits released them both, and the villagers called him "the child of filial devotion."

sentences.zh: 夏汝英，湖南安化人。

translations.literal: Xia Ruying was a native of Anhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Ruying came from Anhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 順治初，遊兵掠其家，汝英九歲，衛母不去左右，遊兵掠汝英去。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi roaming soldiers plundered his home; Ruying was nine and guarded his mother, never leaving her side, but the soldiers carried Ruying off.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi roaming soldiers plundered his home. Ruying was nine and clung to his mother, never leaving her side, but the soldiers carried him off.

sentences.zh: 道中告以母孤苦，乞釋還，賊憐而許之。

translations.literal: On the road he told them his mother was alone and helpless, begged to be released and sent back, and the bandits pitied him and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he told them his mother was alone and helpless and begged to be sent back. The bandits pitied him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 金國選，湖南黔陽人，吳三桂之亂，賊掠其父母去。

translations.literal: Jin Guoxuan was a native of Qianyang in Hunan; during Wu Sangui's rebellion bandits carried off his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guoxuan came from Qianyang in Hunan. During Wu Sangui's rebellion bandits seized his parents.

sentences.zh: 國選七歲，牽衣痛哭，求釋，不得。

translations.literal: Guoxuan was seven; he clutched their clothes and wept bitterly, begging for their release, but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan was seven. He clutched their clothes and wept, begging for their release, but in vain.

sentences.zh: 罵賊，賊哧以白刃，不捨。

translations.literal: He cursed the bandits; they brandished naked blades at him, but he would not let go.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed the bandits. They brandished naked blades at him, but he would not let go.

sentences.zh: 擊以杖，終不捨，乃釋其父母。

translations.literal: They beat him with staves, yet he still would not let go, and at last they released his parents.
translations.idiomatic: They beat him with clubs, yet he still would not let go. At last they released his parents.

sentences.zh: 張愫，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Zhang Su was a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su came from Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，寇至，從其祖走避。

translations.literal: When he was ten bandits came, and he fled with his grandfather to escape.
translations.idiomatic: He was ten when bandits came. He fled with his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 寇執其祖，將殺之，愫哀號求代，身蔽祖，被數創，不顧。

translations.literal: The bandits seized his grandfather and were about to kill him; Su wailed and begged to die in his place, shielded his grandfather with his body, received many wounds, and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized his grandfather and were about to kill him. Su wailed and begged to die in his stead, shielded his grandfather with his body, took many wounds, and did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 寇嗟嘆，舍之去。

translations.literal: The bandits sighed in admiration and let them go.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits sighed in admiration and left them.

sentences.zh: 李志善、志勃，湖南安化人。

translations.literal: Li Zhishan and Zhibo were natives of Anhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhishan and Zhibo came from Anhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父步武。

translations.literal: Their father was Buwu.
translations.idiomatic: Their father was Buwu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 流寇破縣，縛步武，志善十六、志勃十四，

translations.literal: Roaming bandits overran the county and bound Buwu; Zhishan was sixteen and Zhibo fourteen,
translations.idiomatic: Roaming bandits overran the county and bound Buwu. Zhishan was sixteen and Zhibo fourteen,

sentences.zh: 號泣求免。

translations.literal: and they wailed, begging that he be spared.
translations.idiomatic: and they wept, begging that he be spared.

sentences.zh: 賊詰步武里中孰為富，步武罵賊，賊殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits asked Buwu who in the village was rich; Buwu cursed the bandits, and they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits asked Buwu who in the village was wealthy. Buwu cursed them, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 志善、志勃奪賊刀殺賊，皆為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Zhishan and Zhibo seized the bandits' knives and killed bandits, but were themselves killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishan and Zhibo seized the bandits' knives and killed some of them, but were themselves slain.

sentences.zh: 彭大士，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Peng Dashi was a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Dashi came from Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 順治初，李自成餘黨破縣，執大士母求金。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi remnants of Li Zicheng's forces overran the county, seized Dashi's mother, and demanded gold.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, remnants of Li Zicheng's forces overran the county, seized Dashi's mother, and demanded gold.

sentences.zh: 大士紿賊：「金在井側。

translations.literal: Dashi deceived the bandits: "The gold is beside the well."
translations.idiomatic: Dashi deceived the bandits, saying, "The gold is beside the well."

sentences.zh: 」請偕往，因赴井，母走免。

translations.literal: He asked them to go with him, then threw himself into the well, and his mother fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He asked them to come with him, then threw himself into the well. His mother fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 大士年十八，妻仇歸大士僅二十日，亦入井死。

translations.literal: Dashi was eighteen; his wife Qiu had been married to Dashi only twenty days and also threw herself into the well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dashi was eighteen. His wife Qiu had been married to him only twenty days and threw herself into the well as well.

sentences.zh: 錢孝則，江南桐城人。

translations.literal: Qian Xiaozi was a native of Tongcheng in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiaozi came from Tongcheng in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 方明福王時，父以黨人被逮急，變姓名，挈家人亡命至震澤。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, when the Prince of Fu reigned, his father, implicated as a partisan, was urgently arrested; he changed his name, took his family, and fled for his life to Zhenze.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Ming, when the Prince of Fu reigned, his father was seized as a partisan. He changed his name, took his family, and fled to Zhenze.

sentences.zh: 兵起，母及弟、妹皆赴水死，孝則與父匿稻田中得脫。

translations.literal: When war broke out his mother and younger brother and sister all entered the water and died; Xiaozi and his father hid in the rice fields and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When fighting broke out his mother, younger brother, and sister all drowned themselves. Xiaozi and his father hid in the rice fields and survived.

sentences.zh: 兵過，收葬母及弟、妹，走福建。

translations.literal: After the soldiers passed he gathered and buried his mother and younger brother and sister, then fled to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After the soldiers passed he buried his mother, brother, and sister, then fled to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，福建亂作，父子奔避相失。

translations.literal: Before long turmoil broke out in Fujian, and father and son fled separately and lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fujian fell into chaos, and father and son fled separately and lost each other.

sentences.zh: 孝則走廣東，數年還福建，求父十三年，始得與父俱歸。

translations.literal: Xiaozi went to Guangdong; after several years he returned to Fujian and sought his father for thirteen years before at last finding him and returning home together.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozi went to Guangdong. Years later he returned to Fujian and searched for his father for thirteen years before at last finding him and bringing him home.

sentences.zh: 父續娶於徐，徐有富名。

translations.literal: His father remarried a woman of the Xu family, who were famed for wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His father remarried into the Xu family, who were renowned for their wealth.

sentences.zh: 父他往，盜夜至，毀牖，縛孝則迫令導入徐室，孝則不可。

translations.literal: When his father was away robbers came by night, broke the window, bound Xiaozi, and forced him to lead them into the Xu house; Xiaozi refused.
translations.idiomatic: While his father was away, robbers came by night, broke in, bound Xiaozi, and forced him to lead them into the Xu house. He refused.

sentences.zh: 盜斫以斧，顱裂死。

translations.literal: The robbers struck him with an axe and his skull split open—he died.
translations.idiomatic: The robbers struck him with an axe. His skull split open and he died.

sentences.zh: 任遇亨，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Ren Yuheng was a native of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuheng came from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 生有膂力。

translations.literal: From birth he had great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was born with unusual strength.

sentences.zh: 國初盜大起，遇亨負父逃，盜劫其父去。

translations.literal: Early in the dynasty banditry rose greatly; Yuheng carried his father on his back to flee, but bandits seized his father and carried him off.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty banditry flared. Yuheng carried his father on his back to flee, but bandits seized his father.

sentences.zh: 遇亨持刀突入，負父出，身被數創，腸出，遇醫得不死，扶父徙居嘉定以老。

translations.literal: Yuheng seized a knife and burst in, carried his father out on his back, received many wounds with his bowels protruding, met a physician and did not die, supported his father and moved to live at Jiading until old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yuheng seized a knife, rushed in, and carried his father out on his back. He took many wounds and his bowels spilled out, but a physician saved him. He moved with his father to Jiading, where they lived out their years.

sentences.zh: 族子裕德，有土豪積怨於其父，伺隙持刀欲殺之。

translations.literal: His clansman's son Yude—there was a local bully who bore a grudge against Yude's father and, watching for an opening, took a knife intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman's son Yude had an enemy in a local bully who bore a grudge against Yude's father and, watching his chance, drew a knife to kill him.

sentences.zh: 裕德年十一，身蔽父，兩手奪刀，正言曉以禍福，土豪擲刀去。

translations.literal: Yude was eleven; he shielded his father with his body, seized the knife with both hands, and spoke uprightly to show him the consequences of good and ill—the bully threw down the knife and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yude was eleven. He shielded his father with his body, seized the knife with both hands, and spoke plainly of the consequences. The bully threw down the knife and left.

sentences.zh: 父病痢三年，裕德晝夜扶持，躬滌濯污穢。

translations.literal: His father suffered dysentery for three years; Yude supported him day and night and personally washed away the filth.
translations.idiomatic: His father suffered dysentery for three years. Yude nursed him day and night and personally cleaned away the filth.

sentences.zh: 父卒，居喪哀毀。

translations.literal: When his father died he mourned with grief that wasted his body.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned until his health was broken.

sentences.zh: 友於兄，幼即請代兄杖。

translations.literal: He was affectionate toward his elder brother; from childhood he asked to take his brother's beatings for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his elder brother and from childhood asked to take his brother's beatings for him.

sentences.zh: 兄老而無藉，養生送死皆任之甚具。

translations.literal: His brother grew old without support; Yude undertook all care in life and burial with full completeness.
translations.idiomatic: His brother grew old without means of support. Yude provided for him in life and in death with every need met.

sentences.zh: 陸國安，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Lu Guo'an was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guo'an came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父華宇，順治初，縣境寇作，縛華宇入砦，求金以贖。

translations.literal: His father Huayu—in the early Shunzhi reign banditry arose in the county; they bound Huayu and took him into their stronghold, demanding gold for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huayu—in the early Shunzhi reign bandits rose in the county, seized Huayu, and held him in their stronghold for ransom.

sentences.zh: 國安歸自海上，奮入寇砦，馘寇，救華宇歸，被重創，卒無恙。

translations.literal: Guo'an returned from the sea, rushed boldly into the bandit stronghold, slew bandits, rescued Huayu and brought him home; he received grave wounds but in the end was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an returned from the coast, stormed the bandit stronghold, killed bandits, and brought Huayu home. Though gravely wounded, he recovered.

sentences.zh: 徐守質，江南常熟人。

translations.literal: Xu Shouzhi was a native of Changshu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shouzhi came from Changshu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治初，守質與兄基奉母避亂，母老病，兵至，度不能去。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi Shouzhi and his elder brother Ji supported their mother in fleeing the turmoil; their mother was old and ill, and when soldiers came they judged they could not get away.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi Shouzhi and his elder brother Ji fled the turmoil with their mother. She was old and ill, and when soldiers came they knew they could not escape.

sentences.zh: 守質謂基曰：「毋徒死，絕徐氏後。

translations.literal: Shouzhi said to Ji, "Do not die in vain and cut off the Xu line."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi said to Ji, "Do not die for nothing and cut off the Xu line."

sentences.zh: 兄速行，守質當奉母。

translations.literal: "Elder brother, go quickly; Shouzhi will attend to mother."
translations.idiomatic: "Brother, go quickly. I will stay with mother."

sentences.zh: 」基不可。

translations.literal: Ji would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Ji refused.

sentences.zh: 兵迫，守質慍，促基行。

translations.literal: The soldiers pressed close; Shouzhi grew angry and urged Ji to go.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers drew near. Shouzhi grew angry and pressed Ji to flee.

sentences.zh: 守質有妹適袁氏，早寡，攜子與母俱。

translations.literal: Shouzhi had a sister married into the Yuan family who was widowed early; she brought her son and was with their mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi had a sister married to the Yuan family who was widowed young. She brought her son and stayed with their mother.

sentences.zh: 基乃棄妻、子，挾孤甥而遁。

translations.literal: Ji then abandoned his wife and son, took his orphaned nephew in his arms, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then abandoned his wife and son, took his orphaned nephew in his arms, and fled.

sentences.zh: 事定，基還，母與袁氏妹俱自沈井，守質被二創僕，死。

translations.literal: When affairs settled Ji returned; his mother and his Yuan sister both drowned themselves in a well; Shouzhi received two wounds and fell, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When order returned Ji came back. His mother and his Yuan sister had both drowned themselves in a well. Shouzhi had taken two wounds, collapsed, and died.

sentences.zh: 黃簡，字敬之，湖南祁陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Jian, style name Jingzhi, was a native of Qiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jian, whose style was Jingzhi, came from Qiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父用忠，諸生。

translations.literal: His father Yongzhong was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yongzhong was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 簡事親孝，順治十年二月，李定國兵略湖南，其將郝永忠屠祁陽，簡奉父母避兵竹山。

translations.literal: Jian served his parents filially; in the second month of the tenth year of Shunzhi Li Dingguo's army overran Hunan, and his general Hao Yongzhong massacred Qiyang; Jian led his parents to flee the soldiers to Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was filial toward his parents. In the second month of the tenth year of Shunzhi, Li Dingguo's army overran Hunan, and his general Hao Yongzhong slaughtered Qiyang. Jian led his parents to Zhushan to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 母渴，命簡取飲，兵遽至，簡父竄山陽，簡妻張，奉姑竄山陰。

translations.literal: His mother was thirsty and ordered Jian to fetch drink; soldiers suddenly arrived; Jian's father fled to the sunny side of the mountain, and Jian's wife Zhang led her mother-in-law to flee to the shady side.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was thirsty and sent Jian for water. Soldiers suddenly appeared. Jian's father fled to the sunny slope, and Jian's wife Zhang led her mother-in-law to the shady slope.

sentences.zh: 簡取飲至，不見父母，升高望之，見亂兵縛一人置釜上將烹，則其父也。

translations.literal: Jian brought the drink back but could not see his parents; he climbed high and looked out, and saw disorderly soldiers binding a man and placing him on a cauldron to boil—it was his father.
translations.idiomatic: Jian returned with the water but could not find his parents. He climbed higher to look and saw disorderly soldiers binding a man over a cauldron to boil him—it was his father.

sentences.zh: 簡大呼，往乞代，亂兵釋簡父，執簡求賂，不得，遂烹之。

translations.literal: Jian shouted loudly, went forward and begged to die in his place; the disorderly soldiers released Jian's father, seized Jian and demanded a bribe, did not obtain it, and so boiled him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian cried out and rushed forward, begging to die in his father's place. The soldiers released his father, seized Jian, and demanded a bribe. When he had none, they boiled him alive.

sentences.zh: 村民哀簡，名其山湯鑊嶺。

translations.literal: The villagers mourned Jian and named the mountain Boiling Cauldron Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers mourned Jian and named the mountain Boiling Cauldron Ridge.

sentences.zh: 程原學，字奐若，江南儀真人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanxue, style name Huanruo, was a native of Yizhen in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanxue, whose style was Huanruo, came from Yizhen in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，鄭成功兵退，縣人坐連染死者二十餘，原學祖故睢州知州紹儒與焉。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, when Zheng Chenggong's troops withdrew, more than twenty people in the county died from implication in the affair; Yuanxue's grandfather, the former prefect of Suizhou Shaoru, was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, when Zheng Chenggong's army withdrew, more than twenty county residents died from implication in the affair. Yuanxue's grandfather, the former Suizhou prefect Shaoru, was among them.

sentences.zh: 父免死徙塞外，原學以幼留。

translations.literal: His father was spared death but banished beyond the frontier; Yuanxue remained behind because he was young.
translations.idiomatic: His father was spared death but exiled beyond the frontier. Yuanxue remained behind because he was still a child.

sentences.zh: 稍長，將出塞求父，慮死且無後，乃娶妻生子。

translations.literal: When he had grown a little he was about to go beyond the frontier to seek his father; fearing he might die without posterity, he took a wife and had a son.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older he prepared to cross the frontier to find his father. Fearing he might die without an heir, he married and had a son.

sentences.zh: 妻死，挾子行道中，子病，還，計行待子長。

translations.literal: His wife died; he took his son on the road, but the boy fell ill, so he returned, planning to wait until the son had grown before setting out.
translations.idiomatic: His wife died. He set out with his son, but the boy fell ill on the road, so he turned back, planning to wait until the boy was grown.

sentences.zh: 居恆喪服，食但啜粥，不飯，不食果蔬，衣不帛不棉。

translations.literal: He constantly wore mourning garments, ate only gruel and not rice, ate no fruits or vegetables, and wore neither silk nor cotton.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly wore mourning dress, ate only gruel and never rice, took no fruit or vegetables, and wore neither silk nor cotton.

sentences.zh: 僦居學舍旁，授經不出戶。

translations.literal: He rented a dwelling beside a school and taught the classics without leaving his door.
translations.idiomatic: He rented a room beside a school and taught the classics without ever leaving home.

sentences.zh: 訓導顧靄慕其賢，屢過皆不見。

translations.literal: The instructor Gu Ai admired his virtue and visited many times, but Yuanxue never received him.
translations.idiomatic: The instructor Gu Ai admired his character and called on him many times, but Yuanxue never received him.

sentences.zh: 偕其弟子出不意往語原學：「何自苦？

translations.literal: He took his disciples and went unexpectedly to speak to Yuanxue: "Why do you torment yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: He brought his disciples and paid an unexpected visit to Yuanxue, saying, "Why do you make yourself suffer?"

sentences.zh: 」原學對曰：「原學有隱痛，不可以為人，非以自苦也。

translations.literal: Yuanxue replied, "Yuanxue has a hidden grief and cannot face others; it is not that I torment myself."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxue answered, "I bear a private grief and cannot face other people. This is not self-torment."

sentences.zh: 」明日報謁，贄硯與畫，靄謝曰：「子無所受於人，今吾受子遺，亦原以報子。

translations.literal: The next day he came to pay his respects with an inkstone and a painting as gifts; Ai declined, saying, "You accept nothing from others; if I now accept your gift, I wish to repay you in kind."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he called with an inkstone and a painting as gifts. Ai declined, saying, "You take nothing from others. If I accept your gift now, I must repay you in kind."

sentences.zh: 」原學乃持硯與畫去。

translations.literal: Yuanxue then took the inkstone and painting and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxue then took the inkstone and painting and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 他日復過之，已他徙矣。

translations.literal: Another day he passed by again, but Yuanxue had already moved elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed by again another day, Yuanxue had already moved away.

sentences.zh: 俄卒，靄求得其硯，銘曰「廉士硯」。

translations.literal: Soon after Yuanxue died; Ai sought out his inkstone and inscribed it "The Upright Man's Inkstone."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanxue died. Ai found his inkstone and inscribed it "The Upright Man's Inkstone."

sentences.zh: 鬱褒，字子弁，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Yu Bao, style name Zibian, was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bao, whose style was Zibian, came from Jiashan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父之章，順治六年進士，以大理寺丞坐罪徙尚陽堡。

translations.literal: His father Zhizhang, a jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, as an assistant minister of the Court of Judicial Review was convicted and banished to Shangyang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhizhang, who had passed the examinations in the sixth year of Shunzhi, was convicted as a vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and exiled to Shangyang Fort.

sentences.zh: 京師修治官廨，許罪人出家財佐工贖罪，褒請任刑部官廨，之章得贖還。

translations.literal: When the capital repaired government offices, convicts were allowed to contribute family wealth to assist the work and redeem their punishment; Bao asked to undertake the Ministry of Punishments offices, and Zhizhang was ransomed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital repaired government offices, convicts were allowed to pay from family wealth to help the work and redeem their sentences. Bao undertook the Ministry of Punishments project, and Zhizhang was ransomed and came home.

sentences.zh: 工未如程，例當復徙，褒叩閽，請棄官代行。

translations.literal: The work did not meet schedule; by regulation he should be banished again; Bao knocked at the palace gate and asked to abandon office and go in his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: The work fell behind schedule, and by regulation Zhizhang should be exiled again. Bao went to the palace gate and asked to resign his post and go in his father's stead.

sentences.zh: 褒弟諸生廣，叩閽，言身當代父徙，留褒侍父疾。

translations.literal: Bao's younger brother Guang, a licentiate, also knocked at the gate, saying he himself should go in his father's place and leave Bao to nurse their father's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's younger brother Guang, a licentiate, also went to the gate, saying he should go in his father's place and leave Bao to nurse their father.

sentences.zh: 部議子代父徙非舊例，仍用衝突儀仗例治罪。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that a son going in his father's place was not an old precedent, and they still applied the regulation on obstructing an imperial procession to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that a son replacing his father in exile was not precedent, and still punished them under the statute for obstructing an imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 聖祖愍其孝友，並宥之。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor pitied their filial brotherly devotion and pardoned them both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied their filial devotion and pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 之章還鄉里，褒以貢生授江西永豐知縣。

translations.literal: Zhizhang returned to his home district; Bao, as a tribute student, was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhang returned home. Bao, as a tribute student, was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 姚易修，字象亭，江南元和人。

translations.literal: Yao Yixiu, style name Xiangting, was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yixiu, whose style was Xiangting, came from Yuanhe in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父宗甲，康熙初客閩浙總督范承謨幕。

translations.literal: His father Zongjia early in Kangxi served on the staff of Fan Chengmo, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zongjia served early in the Kangxi reign on the staff of Fan Chengmo, governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠為亂，執承謨，盡縶其幕客，宗甲與焉。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong rebelled, seized Chengmo, and imprisoned all his staff—Zongjia among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled he seized Chengmo and imprisoned all his staff, Zongjia included.

sentences.zh: 易修聞，詣精忠，齧指作血書原代父死，賊乃釋宗甲而係易修獄，脅使降，易修不為屈。

translations.literal: When Yixiu heard he went to Jingzhong, bit his finger and wrote a blood letter begging to die in his father's place; the rebels then released Zongjia and bound Yixiu in prison, pressing him to surrender, but Yixiu would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixiu heard, he went to Jingzhong, bit his finger, and wrote a plea in blood offering to die in his father's place. The rebels released Zongjia and imprisoned Yixiu, pressing him to submit, but he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，師至，乃得脫歸。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi the imperial army arrived and he was able to escape and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi the imperial army arrived, and he was able to return home.

sentences.zh: 易修母聞變，悲泣，兩目盲，易修晨起舐母目，母目復明。

translations.literal: Yixiu's mother, hearing of the disaster, wept in grief until both eyes went blind; Yixiu each morning licked his mother's eyes, and her sight returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yixiu's mother, hearing of the disaster, wept until she went blind in both eyes. Each morning Yixiu licked her eyes, and her sight returned.

sentences.zh: 鄰家火，易修突火入，負父出；

translations.literal: When a neighbor's house caught fire Yixiu rushed into the flames and carried his father out;
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's house caught fire, Yixiu rushed into the flames and carried his father out;

sentences.zh: 又入，負母出。

translations.literal: then went in again and carried his mother out.
translations.idiomatic: then went in again and carried his mother out.

sentences.zh: 發盡燎，兩足焦爛，而父母俱無恙。

translations.literal: His hair was burned away and both feet were charred, yet both parents were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: His hair was burned off and both feet were charred, yet both parents were unharmed.

sentences.zh: 胡夢豸，江南江都人。

translations.literal: Hu Mengzhi was a native of Jiangdu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mengzhi came from Jiangdu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，從父至紹興省墓，道遇盜劫民財，斥其不義，盜怒，將刃之。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he accompanied his father to Shaoxing to visit the ancestral tomb; on the road they met bandits robbing the people; he denounced their injustice, and the bandits in anger were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he accompanied his father to Shaoxing to tend the family grave. On the road they met bandits robbing travelers. He denounced them, and the bandits in anger were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 夢豸從後至，奔赴，擊盜僕，民群起毆殺盜。

translations.literal: Mengzhi came from behind, rushed forward, struck the bandit down, and the people rose together and beat the bandit to death.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzhi came up from behind, rushed forward, struck the bandit down, and the crowd rose and beat the man to death.

sentences.zh: 盜大至，欲屠其里，夢豸曰：「不可以我故，危一鄉也。

translations.literal: Bandits came in great force and meant to massacre the village; Mengzhi said, "You must not endanger a whole township because of me."
translations.idiomatic: More bandits came, intending to massacre the village. Mengzhi said, "You must not put a whole township in peril because of me."

sentences.zh: 」入盜寨，獨承殺盜，遂被殺。

translations.literal: He entered the bandit camp, took sole responsibility for killing the bandit, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the bandit camp, took sole blame for killing the man, and was slain.

sentences.zh: 賀上林，江蘇丹陽人。

translations.literal: He Shanglin was a native of Danyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He Shanglin came from Danyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父天敘，以事忤知縣，繫獄，將殺之。

translations.literal: His father Tianxu offended the district magistrate over a matter, was imprisoned, and was about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tianxu offended the district magistrate and was imprisoned, facing execution.

sentences.zh: 上林年十八，謀脫父。

translations.literal: Shanglin was eighteen and plotted to free his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglin was eighteen and plotted to save his father.

sentences.zh: 聞巡撫將上官，涉江溯淮，迎舟呼，騶從呵之，不得前，乃發憤投水，發沒數寸，复躍起大呼。

translations.literal: Hearing the governor was about to pass inspection, he crossed the river and went up the Huai to meet the boat and call out; the outriders shouted him down and he could not advance; in despair he threw himself into the water, sank until only a few inches of hair showed, then leaped up again and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the provincial governor was coming on inspection, he crossed the Yangzi and went up the Huai to meet the boat and call out. The escort drove him back. In despair he threw himself into the water, sank until only a few inches of hair showed, then leaped up and shouted again.

sentences.zh: 巡撫見，令救，已死，檢其衣，得白父冤系狀。

translations.literal: The governor saw, ordered rescue, but he was already dead; searching his clothes they found a petition in blood explaining his father's wrongful imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: The governor saw and ordered a rescue, but Shanglin was already dead. In his clothes they found a petition in blood explaining his father's wrongful imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 巡撫按部黜知縣，釋天敘出獄，鄉人為立賀孝子祠。

translations.literal: The governor on inspection dismissed the magistrate, released Tianxu from prison, and the villagers built a shrine to the Filial Son He.
translations.idiomatic: The governor dismissed the magistrate, freed Tianxu, and the villagers built a shrine to the Filial Son He.

sentences.zh: 何士閥，安徽南陵人。

translations.literal: He Shifa was a native of Nanling in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He Shifa came from Nanling in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 族人破其祖母塚以葬，士閥訟不得直，巡撫檄知縣詣勘，族人持之力，事未定。

translations.literal: Clansmen broke open his grandmother's tomb for a burial; Shifa sued but could not obtain justice; the governor ordered the magistrate to investigate on site, but the clansmen resisted forcibly and the matter was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen broke open his grandmother's tomb for another burial. Shifa sued but could not obtain justice. The governor ordered the magistrate to investigate, but the clansmen resisted and the case remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 士閥慟，觸墓碑，腦裂，死。

translations.literal: Shifa in grief struck the tomb stele; his skull split open and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shifa in grief struck his head against the tomb stele. His skull split open and he died.

sentences.zh: 知縣乃責族人他葬，治其罪，葬士閥，碑曰「義士」。

translations.literal: The magistrate then compelled the clansmen to bury elsewhere, punished their crime, buried Shifa, and set up a stele reading "Righteous Man."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate then forced the clansmen to bury elsewhere, punished them, buried Shifa, and erected a stele reading "Righteous Man."

sentences.zh: 陳嘉謨，江蘇興化人。

translations.literal: Chen Jiamo was a native of Xinghua in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiamo came from Xinghua in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 順治初諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate in the early Shunzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate in the early Shunzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 父弘道，為怨家所誣，系揚州府獄。

translations.literal: His father Hongdao was slandered by an enemy and imprisoned in Yangzhou prefectural jail.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongdao was framed by an enemy and imprisoned in the Yangzhou prefectural jail.

sentences.zh: 獄卒絕其橐饘，嘉謨求見父不得，知怨家計必殺之，乃痛哭禱於神，自沉於水。

translations.literal: The jailers cut off his father's food; Jiamo sought to see his father but could not; knowing the enemy surely meant to kill him, he wept bitterly, prayed to the gods, and drowned himself in the water.
translations.idiomatic: The jailers cut off his father's food. Jiamo could not gain access to see him. Knowing the enemy meant to kill his father, he wept, prayed to heaven, and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 明日，鹽運使得嘉謨訟冤血書，而嘉謨僕又訴失嘉謨。

translations.literal: The next day the salt transport commissioner received Jiamo's petition of injustice written in blood, while Jiamo's servant also reported Jiamo missing.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the salt transport commissioner received Jiamo's petition of injustice written in blood, while his servant reported him missing.

sentences.zh: 求其屍，七日得於鈔關水次，植立風濤中，發上指。

translations.literal: They sought his body; after seven days it was found at the Chaoguan waterfront, standing upright in wind and waves, hair pointing upward.
translations.idiomatic: They searched for his body. After seven days it was found at the customs wharf, standing upright in wind and waves, hair pointing skyward.

sentences.zh: 遂出弘道獄，葬嘉謨，而抵誣告者罪。

translations.literal: Hongdao was then released from prison, Jiamo was buried, and the false accusers were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdao was released from prison, Jiamo was buried, and the false accusers were punished.

sentences.zh: 林長貴、長廣，福建福清人。

translations.literal: Lin Changgui and Chuangguang were natives of Fuqing in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Changgui and Chuangguang came from Fuqing in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父宗正，業曬鹽。

translations.literal: Their father Zongzheng worked in the salt evaporation trade.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Zongzheng worked in the salt evaporation trade.

sentences.zh: 入城，至星橋，海潮暴至，溺死。

translations.literal: Entering the city, when he reached Star Bridge a sudden sea tide came and he drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the city, he reached Star Bridge when a sudden tidal surge swept in and drowned him.

sentences.zh: 長貴聞之，奔救不及，仰天長號，投橋下殉；

translations.literal: Changgui heard, ran to rescue but could not arrive in time, wailed long to heaven, and threw himself from the bridge to die with his father;
translations.idiomatic: Changgui heard and ran to save him but arrived too late. He wailed to heaven and threw himself from the bridge to die with his father;

sentences.zh: 長廣繼至，繞崖痛哭，亦自沉。

translations.literal: Chuangguang came after, walked around the cliff weeping bitterly, and also drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chuangguang came afterward, walked along the cliff weeping, and drowned himself as well.

sentences.zh: 時雍正九年七月。

translations.literal: This was in the seventh month of the ninth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the seventh month of the ninth year of Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 里人憫其孝，收三尸斂焉。

translations.literal: The villagers pitied their filial devotion and gathered the three bodies for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers pitied their devotion and gathered the three bodies for burial.

sentences.zh: 戚弢言，字魏亭，浙江德清人。

translations.literal: Qi Taoyan, style name Weiting, was a native of Deqing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Taoyan, whose style was Weiting, came from Deqing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父麟祥，官翰林院侍講學士。

translations.literal: His father Linxiang served as a Hanlin Academy reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linxiang served as a Hanlin Academy reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 坐事戍寧古塔，弢言從，備艱苦。

translations.literal: Convicted in a case he was banished to Ningguta; Taoyan followed and endured every hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted in a case, he was banished to Ningguta. Taoyan followed him and endured every hardship.

sentences.zh: 麟祥遣令歸就試，成雍正八年進士，除福建連江知縣，勤其官。

translations.literal: Linxiang sent him home to take the examinations; he became a jinshi in the eighth year of Yongzheng, was appointed magistrate of Lianjiang in Fujian, and was diligent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Linxiang sent him home to take the examinations. He passed in the eighth year of Yongzheng, became magistrate of Lianjiang in Fujian, and served diligently.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，赦流人，麟祥不得與，弢言深痛之。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong exiles were pardoned, but Linxiang was not included; Taoyan was deeply pained.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong exiles were pardoned, but Linxiang was not included. Taoyan was deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 總督郝玉麟將入覲，弢言刺指血為書求赦父，詣玉麟​​乞代上，玉麟難之。

translations.literal: Governor-general Hao Yulin was about to go to audience; Taoyan pricked his finger and wrote a letter in blood begging pardon for his father, went to Yulin and begged him to present it, and Yulin found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Hao Yulin was about to go to audience at court. Taoyan pricked his finger and wrote a plea in blood begging pardon for his father, then begged Yulin to present it. Yulin hesitated.

sentences.zh: 弢言叩首持玉麟裾號泣，引佩刀欲自裁，玉麟乃許之。

translations.literal: Taoyan kowtowed, clutched Yulin's robe, and wailed; he drew his belt knife intending to kill himself, and Yulin then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Taoyan kowtowed, clutched Yulin's robe, and wept. He drew his belt knife to kill himself, and Yulin then agreed.

sentences.zh: 詣京師，以弢言書上，高宗憫之，赦麟祥。

translations.literal: Going to the capital he presented Taoyan's letter; the High Ancestor pitied him and pardoned Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he presented Taoyan's letter. The emperor was moved and pardoned Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 麟祥就弢言養連江，明年卒。

translations.literal: Linxiang came to Taoyan and was supported at Lianjiang; the next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Linxiang joined Taoyan at Lianjiang and was cared for there. The next year he died.

sentences.zh: 弢言持喪還，哀甚，亦卒。

translations.literal: Taoyan observed mourning and returned home; grief was overwhelming, and he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Taoyan returned home in mourning, grief overwhelmed him, and he too died.

sentences.zh: 李敬躋，字翼茲，雲南馬龍州人。

translations.literal: Li Jingji, style name Yizi, was a native of Malong Prefecture in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingji, whose style was Yizi, came from Malong Prefecture in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父盛唐，雍正八年進士，官四川松茂道，以所部有罪坐監臨官，戍卜魁。

translations.literal: His father Shengtang, a jinshi of the eighth year of Yongzhi, served as circuit intendant of Songmao in Sichuan; because his subordinates were guilty he was punished as supervising official and banished to Buquei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shengtang, who had passed the examinations in the eighth year of Yongzhi, served as circuit intendant of Songmao in Sichuan. Because his subordinates were guilty he was punished as supervising official and exiled to Buquei.

sentences.zh: 卜魁距雲南萬四千里，敬躋三往省。

translations.literal: Buquei was fourteen thousand li from Yunnan; Jingji went three times to visit.
translations.idiomatic: Buquei was fourteen thousand li from Yunnan. Jingji visited three times.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇暴水，喪其僕馬，徒步行，路人哀之，與之食，導使詣盛唐，盛唐輒令還侍祖母，迫使歸。

translations.literal: Once he met violent floodwaters and lost his servants and horses; he walked on foot; passersby pitied him, gave him food, and guided him to Shengtang, who always ordered him back to attend his grandmother and forced him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met a violent flood and lost his servants and horses. He walked on foot. Travelers pitied him, fed him, and guided him to Shengtang, who always sent him back to care for his grandmother and forced him home.

sentences.zh: 敬躋成乾隆二十二年進士，授福建將樂知縣，計贖盛唐還。

translations.literal: Jingji became a jinshi in the twenty-second year of Qianlong, was appointed magistrate of Jiangle in Fujian, and planned to ransom Shengtang home.
translations.idiomatic: Jingji passed the examinations in the twenty-second year of Qianlong, became magistrate of Jiangle in Fujian, and planned to ransom his father home.

sentences.zh: 盛唐死戍所，敬躋遂發病，日嗚嗚而啼，未幾亦死。

translations.literal: Shengtang died at the place of exile; Jingji then fell ill, whimpered and wept day after day, and soon died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shengtang died in exile. Jingji fell ill, whimpered and wept day after day, and soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 卜魁有范傑者，與盛唐善，盛唐倚以居二十年，至是歸其喪。

translations.literal: At Buquei there was a Fan Jie who was close to Shengtang; Shengtang had relied on him to live for twenty years, and now he brought back the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At Buquei a man named Fan Jie had been Shengtang's close friend for twenty years. He now brought the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 閩人吳阿玉嘗欲從敬躋之官，盛唐喪過京師，吳為送還雲南。

translations.literal: A Fujian man Wu Ayu had wished to follow Jingji to office; when Shengtang's coffin passed through the capital Wu escorted it back to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: A Fujian man named Wu Ayu had wished to follow Jingji to his post. When Shengtang's coffin passed through the capital, Wu escorted it back to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 張大觀，河南偃師人。

translations.literal: Zhang Daguan was a native of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daguan came from Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年秋，伊、洛水溢。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong the Yi and Luo rivers overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong the Yi and Luo rivers flooded.

sentences.zh: 灌偃師，民避水奎星樓上，大觀奉母亦登焉。
