translations.literal: The flood inundated Yanshi; the people took refuge on the Kuixing Tower, and Daguan supporting his mother climbed it as well.
translations.idiomatic: The flood inundated Yanshi. The people took refuge in the Kuixing Tower, and Daguan led his mother up as well.

sentences.zh: 水撼樓，樓傾，柱壓大觀手，臂折，奮入水求母。

translations.literal: The water shook the tower; the tower collapsed; a pillar crushed Daguan's hand and his arm broke; he struggled into the water to seek his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The water shook the tower until it collapsed. A pillar crushed Daguan's hand and broke his arm. He plunged into the water to find his mother.

sentences.zh: 望母髻露水中，得之，負出水，攀樹以上，泳而求食以食母。

translations.literal: He saw his mother's hair-knot showing above the water, found her, carried her out on his back, climbed a tree, swam to seek food and fed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He saw his mother's hair-knot above the water, found her, carried her out on his back, climbed a tree, swam for food, and fed her.

sentences.zh: 水退，負母歸其室，即夕創重死。

translations.literal: When the water receded he carried his mother back to their house, and that same evening died of his grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When the water receded he carried his mother home. That same evening he died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 同時有楊璞，與其弟奉母居。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Yang Pu, who lived with his younger brother supporting their mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Yang Pu, who lived with his younger brother caring for their mother.

sentences.zh: 水至，弟以筏載其妻逃山上，母呼不應。

translations.literal: When the water came his younger brother used a raft to carry his wife and fled to the mountain; their mother called but he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When the flood came his younger brother put his wife on a raft and fled uphill. Their mother called, but he did not answer.

sentences.zh: 璞棄妻子背襁母，浮水至神堤灘，或援之，得登。

translations.literal: Pu abandoned wife and child, carried his mother in swaddling-cloths on his back, floated on the water to Shendi Beach, was helped by someone, and got ashore.
translations.idiomatic: Pu abandoned his wife and child, carried his mother on his back through the water to Shendi Beach, was helped ashore, and climbed to safety.

sentences.zh: 頃之，有婦抱子從水下，母遙望，呼曰：「吾婦與孫也！

translations.literal: Before long a woman holding a child came down the water; the mother looked from afar and cried, "That is my daughter-in-law and grandson!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon a woman holding a child came down the current. From afar the mother cried, "That is my daughter-in-law and grandson!"

sentences.zh: 」拯之，皆不死。

translations.literal: They rescued them, and all survived.
translations.idiomatic: They pulled them out, and all survived.

sentences.zh: 而弟乘筏即至山下，樹折壓筏沉，夫婦俱死。

translations.literal: But the younger brother on his raft had just reached the foot of the mountain when a tree broke, crushed the raft, and it sank—husband and wife both died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother's raft had just reached the foot of the hill when a tree broke, crushed the raft, and sank. Husband and wife both drowned.

sentences.zh: 又有蔡應泰，居母喪，柩在堂。

translations.literal: There was also Cai Yingtai, who was in mourning for his mother with the coffin in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cai Yingtai, mourning his mother with the coffin still in the hall.

sentences.zh: 水至，以繩繫母柩，跪而負之，入水中疾駛，亦至神堤灘。

translations.literal: When the water came he tied a rope to his mother's coffin, knelt and carried it on his back, rushed through the water swiftly, and also reached Shendi Beach.
translations.idiomatic: When the flood came he tied a rope to his mother's coffin, knelt and bore it on his back, and sped through the water to Shendi Beach.

sentences.zh: 村民以長鉤引至岸，舁以上。

translations.literal: Villagers with long hooks drew him to shore and lifted him up.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers hooked him with long poles, pulled him ashore, and lifted him up.

sentences.zh: 日暮，其妻、子亦得救。

translations.literal: At dusk his wife and child were also saved.
translations.idiomatic: By evening his wife and child were saved as well.

sentences.zh: 張士仁，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiren was a native of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiren came from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 六歲，母有疾，泣禱請代，母良愈。

translations.literal: At six his mother fell ill; he wept and prayed to take her place, and his mother soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At six his mother fell ill. He wept and prayed to suffer in her place, and she soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 十三從父寢，仇伏榻下，露刃出。

translations.literal: At thirteen he was sleeping with his father when an enemy hid under the couch and drew a blade.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he was sleeping beside his father when an enemy hid under the bed and drew a blade.

sentences.zh: 士仁呼父未應，手捍之，指欲墮，涕泣語仇請代，仇為感動，呼其父醒，曰：「爾有此子，吾不忍殺爾。

translations.literal: Shiren called to his father but got no answer; he blocked with his hands until his fingers nearly fell off, wept and begged the enemy to kill him instead; the enemy was moved, woke his father, and said, "With a son like this, I cannot bear to kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Shiren called to his father but got no answer. He blocked the blade with his hands until his fingers nearly severed, wept, and begged the man to kill him instead. Moved, the enemy woke his father and said, "With a son like this, I cannot kill you."

sentences.zh: 」父惶遽，良久始定，與矢天日，釋怨。

translations.literal: His father was terrified; only after a long while did he calm down; they swore an oath to heaven and released their enmity.
translations.idiomatic: His father was terrified. Only after a long while did he calm down. They swore an oath before heaven and ended their feud.

sentences.zh: 母喪盡禮，後母虐士仁，士仁孝敬無稍渝，後母亦感悟。

translations.literal: He observed every rite in his mother's mourning; his stepmother abused Shiren, yet Shiren showed filial respect without the slightest change, and his stepmother too came to her senses.
translations.idiomatic: He observed every rite at his mother's funeral. His stepmother abused him, yet he showed her filial respect without change, and she too was moved to repentance.

sentences.zh: 火作，負父出，復入火負後母，後母抱幼子，幾不勝，風反得無恙。

translations.literal: When fire broke out he carried his father out, went back into the flames to carry out his stepmother; his stepmother held a young son and nearly could not endure, but the wind shifted and they were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out he carried his father out, then went back for his stepmother. She held a young son and nearly could not go on, but the wind shifted and all were unharmed.

sentences.zh: 居父及後母喪如喪母，里或忤父母，必泣勸之，悔乃已。

translations.literal: In mourning for his father and stepmother he observed the rites as for his mother; if anyone in the village was disrespectful to parents he would weep and counsel them until they repented.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father and stepmother as he had his mother. If anyone in the village was disrespectful to parents, he wept and urged them until they repented.

sentences.zh: 潘瑂，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Pan Mei was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父出遠遊，家遇火，母出篋令瑂負以行，及門回視，不見母，委篋復入，家人自火出，止瑂毋入，瑂不可，入與母俱死。

translations.literal: His father had gone on a distant journey; fire struck the house; his mother took out a box and told Mei to carry it as they left; at the door she looked back and did not see her mother; she set down the box and went back in; family members coming out of the fire told Mei not to enter, but he would not obey and went in and died with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father was away on a long journey when fire struck the house. His mother handed Mei a box to carry as they fled. At the door she looked back and did not see her mother. Mei set down the box and went back in. Family members fleeing the flames told him not to go in, but he refused and died with his mother.

sentences.zh: 瑂女兄珠姑嫁范氏，歸寧，亦在火中，家人欲掖以出，珠姑揮之曰：「汝男子，何可掖我！

translations.literal: Mei's elder sister Zhugu had married into the Fan family and was visiting home; she too was in the fire; family wanted to help her out, but Zhugu waved them off, saying, "You are men—how can you support me!"
translations.idiomatic: Mei's elder sister Zhugu, married into the Fan family, was visiting home and was caught in the fire. Family tried to help her out, but she waved them off, saying, "You are men—how can you support me!"

sentences.zh: 我從我母死耳。

translations.literal: I will die with my mother, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I will die with my mother."

sentences.zh: 」火熄，瑂與母、姊三尸相環結，時乾隆四十四年十二月望。

translations.literal: When the fire died Mei, his mother, and his sister—the three bodies—were found intertwined; this was on the full moon of the twelfth month of the forty-fourth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire died, Mei, his mother, and his sister were found with their bodies intertwined. This was on the full moon of the twelfth month of the forty-fourth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 瑂聘妻王，家江乾，聞喪來歸，事舅以孝聞。

translations.literal: Mei's betrothed Wang, whose family lived on the riverbank, heard of the mourning and came to marry into the family; she served her father-in-law with filial devotion and was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Mei's betrothed, Wang, whose family lived on the riverbank, heard of the deaths and came to join the household. She served her father-in-law with filial devotion and was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 劉希向，江南山陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Xixiang was a native of Shanyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xixiang came from Shanyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 火，其父入火中求先人木主遺像。

translations.literal: Fire broke out; his father entered the flames to seek the ancestral spirit tablets and portraits.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out, his father entered the flames to recover the ancestral tablets and portraits.

sentences.zh: 希向自外歸，突火入，求其父不得，號而出；

translations.literal: Xixiang returned from outside, dashed into the fire, could not find his father, and wailed as he came out;
translations.idiomatic: Xixiang returned from outside, rushed into the fire, could not find his father, and came out wailing;

sentences.zh: 復入，火方盛，救者以為劉氏父子死矣。

translations.literal: He entered again; the fire was at its height; rescuers thought both father and son of the Liu family were dead.
translations.idiomatic: He went in again while the fire raged. Rescuers assumed both Liu men had perished.

sentences.zh: 俄而牆圮，顧見庭樹下人影往來，乃爭入負其父出，左奉像，右握木主，希向牽父衣，額半焦矣。

translations.literal: Soon a wall collapsed; looking back they saw figures moving under the garden trees; then they rushed in and carried his father out—left hand holding the portrait, right hand gripping the tablet; Xixiang pulled his father's clothes; his forehead was half burned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a wall collapsed. They saw figures moving under the garden trees and rushed in to carry his father out—portrait in his left hand, tablet in his right. Xixiang tugged at his father's clothes. His forehead was half charred.

sentences.zh: 後數年，父病，希向為割股，良愈。

translations.literal: Several years later his father fell ill; Xixiang cut flesh from his thigh for him, and he soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his father fell ill. Xixiang cut flesh from his own thigh to make medicine, and his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 希向年六十，病噎，其子亦割股，刀鈍，肉不決，剪之，乃下，然希向竟不瘳。

translations.literal: Xixiang was sixty and suffered from choking illness; his son also cut flesh from his thigh; the knife was dull and the flesh would not sever, so he cut it with scissors, and the father swallowed it, yet Xixiang never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty Xixiang fell ill with a choking ailment. His son cut flesh from his thigh as well, but the knife was dull and the flesh would not come free, so he trimmed it with scissors until his father could swallow it. Even so, Xixiang never recovered.

sentences.zh: 沈嗣綬，字森甫，江陰人。

translations.literal: Shen Sishou, style name Senfu, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Sishou, whose style was Senfu, came from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 父燿鋆，湖北通判，咸豐二年死於寇。

translations.literal: His father Yaojun served as subprefect of Hubei and died at the hands of bandits in the second year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yaojun served as subprefect of Hubei and was killed by bandits in the second year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 嗣綬奉母還，寇至，徙避江船，高不可攀，展被以其母登。

translations.literal: Sishou brought his mother home; when bandits came they fled to a river boat; it was too high to climb; he spread a quilt and helped his mother aboard.
translations.idiomatic: Sishou brought his mother home. When bandits came they fled to a river boat that was too high to climb. He spread out a quilt and helped his mother aboard.

sentences.zh: 至通州，轉徙山東、河南，結繩床舁母，步從之，千數百里，不去左右。

translations.literal: Reaching Tongzhou they moved on through Shandong and Henan; he made a rope bed to carry his mother and walked after it for more than a thousand li, never leaving her side.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Tongzhou and moved on through Shandong and Henan. He rigged a rope litter to carry his mother and walked beside it for more than a thousand li, never leaving her side.

sentences.zh: 未至蘭山，道遇寇。

translations.literal: Before reaching Lanshan they met bandits on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached Lanshan, they met bandits on the road.

sentences.zh: 嗣綬涕泣乞免，寇感其孝，遣四騎護行。

translations.literal: Sishou wept and begged to be spared; the bandits were moved by his filial devotion and sent four horsemen to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Sishou wept and begged to be spared. The bandits were moved by his devotion and sent four horsemen to escort them.

sentences.zh: 至蘭山，方閉城拒寇，嗣綬求入城，守者疑諜也，趣縛之，涕泣言其故，乃得釋。

translations.literal: At Lanshan the city was closed against the bandits; Sishou asked to enter; the guards suspected him a spy and hurried to bind him; weeping he explained his reason and was then released.
translations.idiomatic: At Lanshan the city was closed against the bandits. Sishou asked to enter, but the guards suspected him of being a spy and moved to bind him. Weeping, he explained his story and was released.

sentences.zh: 既，亦得官湖北，以母病不赴。

translations.literal: Later he also received an appointment in Hubei, but because his mother was ill he did not take it up.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received an appointment in Hubei as well, but did not take it up because his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 侍養十六年，進湯藥，夜起，慮履聲驚母，雖嚴寒必跣。

translations.literal: He attended and supported her for sixteen years, bringing medicine and broth; rising at night he feared the sound of footsteps would startle his mother, and even in severe cold he went barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for her for sixteen years, bringing medicine and broth. When he rose at night he feared the sound of footsteps would startle her, and even in bitter cold he went barefoot.

sentences.zh: 凡事婉曲稱母意，見者感嘆。

translations.literal: In all matters he tactfully pleased his mother's wishes; those who saw it were moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: In everything he tactfully pleased his mother. All who saw it were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 謝君澤，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Xie Junze was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Junze came from Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父祜曾，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Huzeng was renowned for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huzeng was known for his filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 寇亂，為賊虜，君澤冒死依護。

translations.literal: In the bandit turmoil he was captured by rebels; Junze risked death to stay close and protect him.
translations.idiomatic: During the bandit turmoil his father was captured. Junze risked death to stay close and protect him.

sentences.zh: 父齒豁，不能食，恆嚼以哺。

translations.literal: His father's teeth were gone and he could not eat; Junze always chewed food for him and fed him.
translations.idiomatic: His father's teeth were gone and he could not eat. Junze always chewed food for him and fed him by mouth.

sentences.zh: 賊欲戕之，則號泣乞代父死，賊首感動，並釋之。

translations.literal: When the rebels meant to kill him, Junze wailed and begged to die in his father's place; the rebel chief was moved and released them both.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels meant to kill his father, Junze wailed and begged to die in his place. The rebel chief was moved and released them both.

sentences.zh: 馮福基，代州人。

translations.literal: Feng Fuji was a native of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fuji came from Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 父焯，為安徽潛山天堂司巡檢。

translations.literal: His father Chao served as assistant inspector of Tiantang in Qianshan, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao was assistant inspector of Tiantang in Qianshan, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，寇至，福基年十四，匿母他所，藏利刃，計伺隙殺賊，不可得。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng bandits came; Fuji was fourteen; he hid his mother elsewhere, concealed a sharp blade, and planned to seize an opening to kill the bandits, but could not.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng bandits came. Fuji was fourteen. He hid his mother elsewhere, kept a sharp blade hidden, and planned to kill the bandits when he could, but found no opening.

sentences.zh: 日夜涕泣從至黃梅，市毒藥置飯中，斃賊十七，亦吞藥死。

translations.literal: Weeping day and night he followed them to Huangmei, bought poison and put it in the food, killing seventeen bandits, and also swallowed the poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping day and night he followed them to Huangmei, bought poison and put it in their food, killing seventeen bandits. He then swallowed the poison himself and died.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李續宜奏言：「福基以童穉之年，護母陷賊，計殺兇黨多人，從容就義。

translations.literal: Governor Li Xuyi memorialized: "At a tender age Fuji protected his mother when she fell into the bandits' hands, plotted to kill many of the murderous gang, and calmly accepted death."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Xuyi memorialized: "Though still a child, Fuji protected his mother when she fell into bandit hands, plotted to kill many of the murderous gang, and calmly accepted death."

sentences.zh: 奇節至性，深可嘉愍！

translations.literal: His extraordinary integrity and utmost devotion are deeply worthy of praise and pity!"
translations.idiomatic: His extraordinary courage and filial devotion are deeply worthy of praise and pity!"

sentences.zh: 」被旨旌卹。

translations.literal: An imperial decree honored and compensated him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued a decree honoring and compensating him.

sentences.zh: 黃向堅，字端木，江南吳縣人。

translations.literal: Huang Xiangjian, style name Duanmu, was a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xiangjian, whose style was Duanmu, came from Wu County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父孔昭，崇禎間，官雲南大姚知縣，挈孥之官，向堅獨留。

translations.literal: His father Kongzhao, in the Chongzhen reign, served as magistrate of Dayao in Yunnan; he took wife and children to his post, and Xiangjian alone remained behind.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kongzhao served as magistrate of Dayao in Yunnan during the Chongzhen reign. He took his wife and children to his post, and Xiangjian alone remained behind.

sentences.zh: 鼎革後，孔昭阻兵不得歸，向堅日夜哭，將入雲南，親朋、妻子頗危之，向堅決行。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change Kongzhao was blocked by warfare and could not return; Xiangjian wept day and night and was about to enter Yunnan; kin, friends, and his wife all feared for him, but Xiangjian was resolved to go.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic change Kongzhao was cut off by warfare and could not return. Xiangjian wept day and night and set out for Yunnan. Kin, friends, and his wife all feared for him, but he would not be deterred.

sentences.zh: 至白鹽井，得父母並弟向嚴皆無恙，留一年乃歸，時為順治十年。

translations.literal: Reaching Baiyan Well he found his parents and his younger brother Xiangyan all safe and well; he stayed a year before returning, in the tenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiyan Well he found his parents and his younger brother Xiangyan all safe and well. He stayed a year before returning home, in the tenth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 行二萬五千里有奇，向堅次山川道途所經，自為圖十二記之，吳人作樂府紀其事。

translations.literal: He traveled more than twenty-five thousand li; Xiangjian arranged the mountains, rivers, and roads he passed in order and made twelve maps to record them; the people of Wu wrote ballads to commemorate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He had traveled more than twenty-five thousand li. Xiangjian charted the mountains, rivers, and roads he had passed and made twelve maps to record them. The people of Wu wrote ballads to commemorate his journey.

sentences.zh: 顧廷琦，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Gu Tingqi was a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Tingqi came from Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父繩詒，崇禎間，官四川仁壽知縣，死張獻忠之難。

translations.literal: His father Shengshi, in the Chongzhen reign, served as magistrate of Renshou in Sichuan and died in Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shengshi served as magistrate of Renshou in Sichuan during the Chongzhen reign and died in Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事定，廷琦徒步入四川，閱四年，乃至成都。

translations.literal: When the turmoil ended Tingqi walked on foot into Sichuan; after four years he finally reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the turmoil ended Tingqi walked on foot into Sichuan. After four years he finally reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 展轉求得繩詒墓龍腦橋側，持喪歸，自撰入蜀記述其事。

translations.literal: After much searching he found Shengshi's tomb beside Longnao Bridge, brought the coffin home in mourning, and wrote an account of entering Shu to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: After much searching he found Shengshi's tomb beside Longnao Bridge, brought the coffin home, and wrote an account of his journey into Shu.

sentences.zh: 李澄，字仲瀾，雲南昆陽人。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, style name Zhonglan, was a native of Kunyang in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, whose style was Zhonglan, came from Kunyang in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 明季，充選拔貢生。

translations.literal: In the late Ming he served as a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming he was a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 父兆旂，官廬江訓導，死寇難，幼子淳從死。

translations.literal: His father Zhaoqi served as instructor of Lujiang, died in the bandit turmoil, and his youngest son Chun died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaoqi was instructor of Lujiang, died in the bandit turmoil, and his youngest son Chun died with him.

sentences.zh: 澄奔赴，收父骨返葬，請於當事，得立祠，晨必詣祠拜且泣。

translations.literal: Cheng rushed there, gathered his father's bones and returned to bury them, petitioned the authorities and obtained a shrine, and every morning he went to the shrine to bow and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng rushed there, gathered his father's bones and returned to bury them, petitioned the authorities to establish a shrine, and every morning went to bow and weep before it.

sentences.zh: 寇至，奉母洪避山谷。

translations.literal: When bandits came he took his mother Hong to hide in the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came he led his mother Hong to hide in the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 洪病亟，言不原以山谷終，負母投佛寺，遽卒，負遺骸攢祖墓。

translations.literal: Hong fell gravely ill and said she did not wish to end her days in the mountain valleys; he carried his mother to a Buddhist temple; she suddenly died; he carried her remains and placed them in the ancestral tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fell gravely ill and said she did not wish to die in the mountains. He carried her to a Buddhist temple, where she suddenly died. He then placed her remains in the ancestral tomb.

sentences.zh: 順治初，山倮入州城，劫官舍，發藏粟。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi mountain tribesmen entered the prefectural city, raided government offices, and broke open stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, mountain tribesmen entered the prefectural city, raided government offices, and broke open stored grain.

sentences.zh: 省吏以兵至，執澄將殺之，兵中有識澄者，乃免。

translations.literal: Provincial clerks came with troops, seized Cheng and were about to kill him; among the soldiers was one who knew Cheng, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial clerks came with troops, seized Cheng, and were about to kill him. A soldier who knew him intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 澄因言：「山倮迫飢寒，無與百姓事。

translations.literal: Cheng then said, "The mountain tribesmen are driven by hunger and cold and have no quarrel with the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "The mountain tribesmen are driven by hunger and cold and have no quarrel with the common people."

sentences.zh: 今固不宜累百姓，即山倮亦不宜輕言剿，否則且反戈。

translations.literal: Now it is certainly wrong to burden the common people, and it is also wrong lightly to speak of exterminating the tribesmen, or they will turn their blades back.
translations.idiomatic: It is wrong to burden the common people, and it is also wrong to speak lightly of exterminating the tribesmen, or they will turn against us.

sentences.zh: 」乃坐其渠，州民以安。

translations.literal: They then punished the ringleaders, and the people of the prefecture were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The ringleaders were punished, and the people of the prefecture were at peace.

sentences.zh: 兄弟凡八，與仲弟俱，老，相友愛。

translations.literal: There were eight brothers in all; he and his second younger brother, both old, were deeply affectionate toward each other.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight brothers in all. He and his second younger brother, both in old age, remained deeply devoted to each other.

sentences.zh: 劉獻煜，字台凝，陝西華陰人。

translations.literal: Liu Xianyu, style name Taining, was a native of Huayin in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xianyu, whose style was Taining, came from Huayin in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父濯翼，明崇禎間官武昌，母與偕，遘亂絕消息。

translations.literal: His father Zhuoyi, in the Chongzhen reign of Ming, served at Wuchang; his mother went with him; they met turmoil and all word was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuoyi served at Wuchang during the Chongzhen reign of Ming. His mother went with him, but turmoil cut off all word of them.

sentences.zh: 順治初，獻煜徒步求父母，亂初定，道​​阻，屢瀕險乃達。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi Xianyu went on foot to seek his parents; the turmoil had just settled, the roads were blocked, and he repeatedly faced peril before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi Xianyu set out on foot to find his parents. The turmoil had just settled, the roads were blocked, and he repeatedly faced peril before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 哭山徑中，遇叟識濯翼殯所，發得磚，硃書姓名里貫皆具，猶濯翼所自記也。

translations.literal: Weeping on a mountain path he met an old man who knew Zhuoyi's burial place; opening the tomb he found a brick with name and native place all written in cinnabar—it was still Zhuoyi's own record.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping on a mountain path he met an old man who knew Zhuoyi's burial place. Opening the tomb he found a brick inscribed in cinnabar with name and native place—it was still Zhuoyi's own record.

sentences.zh: 乃負骨歸葬。

translations.literal: He then carried the bones home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the bones home and buried them.

sentences.zh: 錢美恭，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Qian Meigong was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Meigong came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父士驌，明官雲南陽宗知縣，與妾之官，美恭留侍母。

translations.literal: His father Shiji, an official of Ming, served as magistrate of Yangzong in Yunnan; he took a concubine to his post, and Meigong remained to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shiji, a Ming official, served as magistrate of Yangzong in Yunnan. He took a concubine to his post, and Meigong remained to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，美恭得請於母，求父，至雲南，乃知士驌遷嵩明知州，卒葬通海。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi Meigong obtained his mother's permission and went to seek his father; reaching Yunnan he learned Shiji had been transferred to magistrate of Songming, died, and was buried at Tonghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi Meigong obtained his mother's permission and went to seek his father. In Yunnan he learned Shiji had been transferred to Songming, died, and was buried at Tonghai.

sentences.zh: 美恭至通海，得故僕導詣士驌墓，得庶母及幼弟。

translations.literal: Meigong reached Tonghai; an old servant guided him to Shiji's tomb, and he found his concubine mother and young brother.
translations.idiomatic: Meigong reached Tonghai. An old servant guided him to Shiji's tomb, where he found his concubine mother and young brother.

sentences.zh: 貧無貲，留五年，乃負骨歸葬。

translations.literal: Poor and without funds, he stayed five years before carrying the bones home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to travel, he stayed five years before carrying the bones home for burial.

sentences.zh: 趙萬全，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Wanquan was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wanquan came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父應麟，明季客授北遊，萬全始二歲。

translations.literal: His father Yinglin, in the late Ming, went north as a guest teacher; Wanquan was only two.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yinglin went north as a guest teacher in the late Ming when Wanquan was only two.

sentences.zh: 既長，問母：「父安在？

translations.literal: When he grew up he asked his mother, "Where is Father?"
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he asked his mother, "Where is my father?"

sentences.zh: 」母告以故。

translations.literal: His mother told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 年十九，出求父。

translations.literal: At nineteen he went out to seek his father.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he set out to find his father.

sentences.zh: 應麟初客京師，遇亂轉徙死馬邑。

translations.literal: Yinglin had first been a guest teacher in the capital; meeting turmoil he wandered and died at Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglin had first been a guest teacher in the capital. Caught in the turmoil, he wandered and died at Mayi.

sentences.zh: 萬全遍訪江、淮間，亦至京師，心疑應麟死，見道有遺骸，刺血滲之，不得入，則號於路。

translations.literal: Wanquan searched throughout the Yangzi and Huai regions and also reached the capital; suspecting Yinglin was dead, when he saw abandoned remains on the road he pricked his finger and let blood seep in; if it did not soak in he wailed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wanquan searched throughout the Yangzi and Huai regions and also reached the capital. Suspecting his father was dead, whenever he saw abandoned remains on the road he pricked his finger and let blood seep into the bones. If it did not soak in, he wailed in the road.

sentences.zh: 又自京師西，亦至馬邑。

translations.literal: Then from the capital he went west and also reached Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital he went west and also reached Mayi.

sentences.zh: 馬邑人張文義，嘗招應麟主書者，死為之殯。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenyi of Mayi had once invited Yinglin to keep his accounts; when he died Wenyi had him buried.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenyi of Mayi had once hired Yinglin to keep his accounts. When Yinglin died Wenyi had him buried.

sentences.zh: 一日遇萬全，問得其事，導至殯所，慟絕良久，乃裹應麟骨負以歸。

translations.literal: One day he met Wanquan, learned his story, and guided him to the burial place; Wanquan was stricken with grief for a long while, then wrapped Yinglin's bones and carried them home on his back.
translations.idiomatic: One day he met Wanquan, learned his story, and guided him to the burial place. Wanquan was stricken with grief for a long while, then wrapped his father's bones and carried them home on his back.

sentences.zh: 既卒，吏為之祠，琢石表異孝。

translations.literal: After he died officials built him a shrine and carved a stone to mark his extraordinary filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: After his death officials built him a shrine and erected a stone to mark his extraordinary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 劉龍光，字蓼蕭，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Liu Longguang, style name Liaoxiao, was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Longguang, whose style was Liaoxiao, came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父廷諤，仕明為益王長史。

translations.literal: His father Ting'e served Ming as chief secretary to the Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ting'e served the Ming as chief secretary to the Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 師下江西，克建昌，益王遁，廷諤逃山中。

translations.literal: When the army descended on Jiangxi and took Jianchang, the Prince of Yi fled and Ting'e escaped into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army descended on Jiangxi and took Jianchang, the Prince of Yi fled and Ting'e escaped into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 龍光以應試家居，聞亂疾作。

translations.literal: Longguang was at home preparing for the examinations; hearing of the turmoil illness seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Longguang was at home preparing for the examinations. Hearing of the turmoil he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 居五年，乃行詣建昌，不得父母所在。

translations.literal: After five years he set out for Jianchang but could not learn where his parents were.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he set out for Jianchang but could not discover where his parents were.

sentences.zh: 禱於神，夢聞人語在石際，諮石際所在，有女僧示以路。

translations.literal: He prayed to the gods; in a dream he heard a voice say "at Shiji"; asking where Shiji was, a nun showed him the way.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed to the gods. In a dream he heard a voice say "at Shiji." When he asked where Shiji was, a nun showed him the way.

sentences.zh: 行小徑萬山中，經藤峽至白石嶺。

translations.literal: He took a small path through ten thousand mountains, passed Teng Gorge, and reached Baishi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He followed a small path through ten thousand mountains, passed Teng Gorge, and reached Baishi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 徑絕險，攀援顛頓，蒲伏上下。

translations.literal: The path was utterly perilous; he climbed and stumbled, crawling up and down.
translations.idiomatic: The path was utterly perilous. He climbed and stumbled, crawling up and down.

sentences.zh: 嶺盡至石際，於村民姚氏家遇其母，廷諤已前一年卒。

translations.literal: At the end of the ridge he reached Shiji and at the home of a villager surnamed Yao met his mother; Ting'e had died the year before.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the ridge he reached Shiji and at the home of a villager surnamed Yao met his mother. Ting'e had died the year before.

sentences.zh: 居數月，輿櫬奉母歸。

translations.literal: After several months he placed the coffin on a litter and brought his mother home.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he put the coffin on a litter and brought his mother home.

sentences.zh: 所居村曰見娘堡，相傳宋王龍山於此遇母，故得名云。

translations.literal: The village where he lived was called Jianniang Fort; tradition says the Song prince Longshan met his mother here, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The village where he lived was called Jianniang Fort. Tradition says the Song prince Longshan met his mother there, hence the name.

sentences.zh: 李芳巇，小字葵生，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Li Fangxi, courtesy name Kuisheng, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fangxi, whose courtesy name was Kuisheng, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 明季流寇至，湘鄉當孔道，三復三陷，芳巇父母皆被掠。

translations.literal: In the late Ming roving bandits came; Xiangxiang lay on a major route and was taken and lost three times; Fangxi's parents were both carried off.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming roving bandits came. Xiangxiang lay on a major route and was taken and lost three times. Fangxi's parents were both carried off.

sentences.zh: 兄弟死於兵者三，芳巇收葬之，棄家，求父母所在。

translations.literal: Three brothers died in the warfare; Fangxi gathered and buried them, abandoned his home, and sought where his parents were.
translations.idiomatic: Three brothers died in the warfare. Fangxi gathered and buried them, abandoned his home, and set out to find his parents.

sentences.zh: 行數年至貴陽，遇鄉人必為言父狀，或謂軍中某所頗有狀似所言者，詣求之，果得父。

translations.literal: Traveling several years he reached Guiyang; whenever he met a fellow townsman he described his father's appearance; someone said a man in a certain army camp closely matched the description; he went to seek him and indeed found his father.
translations.idiomatic: After several years of travel he reached Guiyang. Whenever he met a fellow townsman he described his father's appearance. Someone said a man in a certain army camp closely matched the description. He went to seek him and indeed found his father.

sentences.zh: 父脫軍中籍與歸。

translations.literal: His father left the army rolls and returned with him.
translations.idiomatic: His father left the army rolls and returned home with him.

sentences.zh: 再出，又數年至寶慶，暮投山家宿，見二嫗操作，其一方理炊，乃似母。

translations.literal: He set out again; after several more years he reached Baoqing; at dusk he lodged at a mountain home and saw two old women at work; one preparing food looked like his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He set out again. After several more years he reached Baoqing. At dusk he lodged at a mountain home and saw two old women at work. One preparing food looked like his mother.

sentences.zh: 芳巇自陳尋母狀，嫗聞遽呼曰：「汝葵生耶？

translations.literal: Fangxi explained his search for his mother; the old woman hearing this cried out at once, "Are you Kuisheng?"
translations.idiomatic: Fangxi explained that he was searching for his mother. The old woman cried out at once, "Are you Kuisheng?"

sentences.zh: 吾即汝母也！

translations.literal: I am your mother!"
translations.idiomatic: It is I, your mother!"

sentences.zh: 」蓋母避兵轉徙，方從此嫗為傭，遂奉母還。

translations.literal: His mother had fled the warfare and wandered, and was just then working as a servant for this old woman; he then brought his mother home.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had fled the warfare and was then working as a servant for this old woman. He brought her home.

sentences.zh: 唐肇虞，江南人，失其縣。

translations.literal: Tang Zhaoyu was a man of Jiangnan; his native county is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhaoyu was from Jiangnan; his native county is no longer recorded.

sentences.zh: 父卒，肇虞尚幼，晝夜哭。

translations.literal: When his father died Zhaoyu was still young and wept day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died Zhaoyu was still a child and wept day and night.

sentences.zh: 母止之，曰：「母哭，能止兒勿哭耶？

translations.literal: His mother tried to stop him, saying, "If a mother weeps, can she stop her child from weeping?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother tried to stop him, saying, "When a mother weeps, how can she keep her child from weeping?"

sentences.zh: 」順治初，江南寇大起，母被掠。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi bandits rose greatly in Jiangnan and his mother was carried off.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi bandits rose throughout Jiangnan and his mother was carried off.

sentences.zh: 肇虞遍求諸村落及旁郡縣，渡江北，复南行數千里，屢與寇遇，僅乃免，卒不得母。

translations.literal: Zhaoyu searched every village and neighboring prefecture and county, crossed north of the river, then traveled south again for several thousand li, repeatedly met bandits and barely escaped, and in the end could not find his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyu searched every village and neighboring prefecture and county, crossed north of the river, then traveled south again for several thousand li, repeatedly met bandits and barely escaped, yet in the end could not find his mother.

sentences.zh: 至江寧，眾問所自來，泣以情告。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangning the crowd asked where he came from; weeping he told them his story.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jiangning the crowd asked where he came from. Weeping, he told them his story.

sentences.zh: 一嫗前問曰：「若母非戴姓

translations.literal: An old woman stepped forward and asked, "Is your mother not surnamed Dai
translations.idiomatic: An old woman stepped forward and asked, "Is your mother surnamed Dai

sentences.zh: 耶？

translations.literal: He said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "It is."

sentences.zh: 」嫗引至家，則其母在焉，相見大慟，遂侍母歸。

translations.literal: The old woman led him to her home, and his mother was there; they met and wept bitterly, and he then attended his mother home.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman led him to her home, where his mother was waiting. They met and wept bitterly, and he then returned home to serve his mother.

sentences.zh: 繆士毅，江南天長人。

translations.literal: Mu Shi Yi, a native of Tianchang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Shi Yi was a native of Tianchang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父廊賓，富。

translations.literal: His father Langbin was wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Langbin was wealthy.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，寇掠其家牛馬，怨家誣以助寇，廊賓見法，妻子徙奉天。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi, bandits plundered the family's cattle and horses; an enemy falsely accused them of aiding the bandits; Langbin was executed by law, and his wife and children were exiled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi, bandits plundered the family's cattle and horses. An enemy falsely accused them of aiding the bandits; Langbin was executed, and his wife and children were exiled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 士毅以後世父得免，依從母以長。

translations.literal: Shi Yi was spared because his adoptive father was not implicated; he grew up relying on his adoptive mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi was spared because his adoptive father was not implicated, and he grew up under his adoptive mother's care.

sentences.zh: 既聞父死母徙狀，從母語之曰：「而母將行，抱汝乳，且言兒僅此一乳，乳當飽，生死與兒訣矣！

translations.literal: When he learned that his father had died and his mother had been exiled, his adoptive mother told him, "When your mother was about to leave, she held you to nurse and said, 'My child has only this one breast of milk—drink your fill, for this is our parting in life and death!'"
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that his father had died and his mother had been exiled, his adoptive mother told him, "When your mother was about to leave, she held you to nurse and said, 'My child has only this one breast—drink your fill, for this is our parting in life and death!'"

sentences.zh: 」士毅聞，號泣，欲行求母，恐去不得還，先娶妻生子，康熙二十二年乃決行。

translations.literal: When Shi Yi heard this, he wailed. He wished to go seek his mother but feared that if he left he might not return, so he first took a wife and had a son; only in the twenty-second year of Kangxi did he resolve to set out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Yi heard this, he wailed. He longed to go seek his mother but feared he might never return, so he first married and had a son. Only in the twenty-second year of Kangxi did he resolve to set out.

sentences.zh: 至瀋陽，遇族人同徙者，知母在烏喇為流人薛氏妻。

translations.literal: Reaching Shenyang, he met a clansman who had been exiled with them and learned that his mother was in Wula, wife of the exiled man surnamed Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Shenyang, he met a clansman who had been exiled with them and learned that his mother was in Wula, married to an exiled man surnamed Xue.

sentences.zh: 乃行求得母，母不相識，士毅具言姓名及兩女兄適誰某，皆信，相抱哭，觀者多流涕。

translations.literal: He traveled on and found his mother. She did not recognize him, but Shi Yi gave full account of his name and the men to whom his two elder sisters had married, and all was credible; they embraced and wept, and many onlookers shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled on and found his mother, though she did not recognize him. Shi Yi gave a full account of his name and the men his two elder sisters had married, and all was credible. They embraced and wept, and many onlookers shed tears.

sentences.zh: 母於法不得還，乃辭歸。

translations.literal: His mother could not return by law, so he took leave and went home.
translations.idiomatic: His mother could not return home by law, so he took leave and went back.

sentences.zh: 居數年，復往，母又徙愛琿。

translations.literal: After several years he went again, and his mother had been moved to Aihui.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he went again, only to learn his mother had been moved to Aihui.

sentences.zh: 行未至，聞母死，求得母葬所，遂居其側僧廬，不復歸。

translations.literal: Before he reached her, he heard his mother had died. He found her burial place and then lived in a monk's cell beside it, never returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached her, he heard his mother had died. He found her burial place and lived in a monk's cell beside it, never returning home.

sentences.zh: 子秉文，長，躬至愛琿，泣請歸，士毅終不可。

translations.literal: His son Bingwen, when grown, went in person to Aihui and wept, begging him to return, but Shi Yi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Bingwen came of age, he went in person to Aihui and wept, begging his father to return, but Shi Yi would not agree.

sentences.zh: 又數年，卒母葬所。

translations.literal: Several years later he died at his mother's burial place.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died at his mother's burial place.

sentences.zh: 秉文乃發祖母瘞，並持父骨還葬。

translations.literal: Bingwen then opened his grandmother's reburial site and also carried his father's bones back for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen then opened his grandmother's reburial site and carried his father's bones home for burial as well.

sentences.zh: 陸承祺，字又祉，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Lu Chenggui, styled Youzhi, a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chenggui, styled Youzhi, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父夢蘭，客死鬱林。

translations.literal: His father Menglan died abroad in Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Menglan died abroad in Yulin.

sentences.zh: 方軍興，逾年乃得問。

translations.literal: War had just broken out, and more than a year passed before they could inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: War had just broken out, and more than a year passed before they could inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 承祺與弟承祚號慟，走萬里，歷險阻，僅得達。

translations.literal: Chenggui and his younger brother Chengzuo wailed in grief and traveled ten thousand li through peril and hardship, barely reaching there.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggui and his younger brother Chengzuo wailed in grief and traveled ten thousand li through peril and hardship, barely reaching their destination.

sentences.zh: 睹叢箐中敗棺，刺血漉骨皆不入，兄弟哭愈哀。

translations.literal: They saw a broken coffin in the thicketed bamboo; they pricked their fingers and let blood drip on the bones, but it would not soak in. The brothers wept all the more bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: They found a broken coffin in the thicketed bamboo. They pricked their fingers and let blood drip on the bones, but it would not soak in, and the brothers wept all the more bitterly.

sentences.zh: 途中有知夢蘭者，告其棺在佛寺，兄弟從以往，撫棺慟，皆隕絕，觀者嗟嘆呼孝子。

translations.literal: On the road someone who had known Menglan told them his coffin was in a Buddhist temple. The brothers followed him there and, embracing the coffin, wept in anguish until both collapsed unconscious; onlookers sighed in admiration and called them filial sons.
translations.idiomatic: On the road someone who had known Menglan told them his coffin was in a Buddhist temple. The brothers went there and, embracing the coffin, wept in anguish until both collapsed unconscious. Onlookers sighed in admiration and called them filial sons.

sentences.zh: 持水飲之，承祚

translations.literal: Someone held water for them to drink; Chengzuo
translations.idiomatic: Someone held water for them to drink. Chengzuo

sentences.zh: 徐甦，承祺氣結不屬，竟死。

translations.literal: gradually revived, but Chenggui's breath remained blocked and he could not recover, and in the end he died.
translations.idiomatic: gradually revived, but Chenggui's breath remained blocked and he could not recover, and in the end he died.

sentences.zh: 承祚匱兩骸擔以歸。

translations.literal: Chengzuo placed both sets of remains in coffins and carried them home on his shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzuo placed both sets of remains in coffins and carried them home on his shoulder.

sentences.zh: 母王得承祚報，知得夢蘭骨及承祺死狀，悲慟不食，七日，未見承祚歸，遽卒。

translations.literal: Their mother Wang received Chengzuo's report, learned that Menglan's bones had been recovered and of Chenggui's death, and grieved so bitterly she would not eat. On the seventh day, before Chengzuo returned, she suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother Wang received Chengzuo's report, learned that Menglan's bones had been recovered and that Chenggui had died, and grieved so bitterly she would not eat. On the seventh day, before Chengzuo returned, she suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 汪龍，江南歙縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Long, a native of She County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Long was a native of She County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 祖客死蘇州，父往迎喪，溺採石，龍時六歲。

translations.literal: His grandfather died as a guest in Suzhou; his father went to bring back the coffin and drowned at Caishi; Long was then six years old.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather died as a guest in Suzhou. His father went to bring back the coffin and drowned at Caishi when Long was six years old.

sentences.zh: 稍長，聞祖喪未歸，如蘇州求祖柩，無知者。

translations.literal: When he grew a little older, learning his grandfather's coffin had not been brought home, he went to Suzhou to seek it, but no one knew where it was.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older and learned his grandfather's coffin had not been brought home, he went to Suzhou to seek it, but no one knew where it was.

sentences.zh: 久之，遇灌園叟與徙其祖柩，引詣殯舍，諸柩縱橫，匍匐諦審，柩有祖名，乃奉以歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he met an old gardener who had helped move his grandfather's coffin; the man led him to the undertaker's hall, where coffins lay scattered about. Long crawled among them and scrutinized each closely; finding one bearing his grandfather's name, he took it home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he met an old gardener who had helped move his grandfather's coffin. The man led him to the undertaker's hall, where coffins lay scattered about. Long crawled among them and scrutinized each one until he found one bearing his grandfather's name, and took it home.

sentences.zh: 龍侍母孝，一夕，疽發背，委頓甚，自力勿使母聞，越數旬始瘥，母竟未知也。

translations.literal: Long served his mother filially. One night a carbuncle broke out on his back and he grew very weak, yet by his own strength he kept his mother from hearing of it; only after several ten-day periods did he recover, and his mother never knew.
translations.idiomatic: Long served his mother filially. One night a carbuncle broke out on his back and he grew very weak, yet he kept his mother from hearing of it. Only after several weeks did he recover, and his mother never knew.

sentences.zh: 方如珽，休寧人。

translations.literal: Fang Ruting, a native of Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ruting was a native of Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 國初，其曾祖避兵客死潛山。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, his great-grandfather, fleeing war, died as a guest in Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty, his great-grandfather fled the war and died as a guest in Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 祖前卒，父不在側，道梗，喪未歸。

translations.literal: His grandfather had died earlier, his father was not present, the roads were blocked, and the remains were not brought home.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had died earlier while his father was absent; the roads were blocked, and the remains were not brought home.

sentences.zh: 如珽既長，問老婢，言有族姑嫁程氏。

translations.literal: When Ruting grew up, he asked an old servant woman, who said there was a clan aunt married to the Cheng family.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruting grew up, he asked an old servant woman, who told him of a clan aunt married into the Cheng family.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，訪之，則嘗會其曾祖喪。

translations.literal: She was over seventy; he visited her, and she had attended his great-grandfather's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: She was over seventy. He visited her and learned she had attended his great-grandfather's funeral.

sentences.zh: 偕往踪跡，至黃石坂，於洞中得敗棺，得白金簪，族姑驗之，其曾祖斂時物也。

translations.literal: Together they traced the trail to Huangshi Slope, where in a cave they found a broken coffin and a silver hairpin; the clan aunt examined it—it was an object from his great-grandfather's encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: Together they traced the trail to Huangshi Slope, where in a cave they found a broken coffin and a silver hairpin. The clan aunt examined it and confirmed it was from his great-grandfather's encoffining.

sentences.zh: 乃負骨歸葬，距其曾祖卒時，已五十有六年矣。

translations.literal: He then carried the bones home for burial, fifty-six years after his great-grandfather's death.
translations.idiomatic: He then carried the bones home for burial, fifty-six years after his great-grandfather's death.

sentences.zh: 張燾，福建連江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tao, a native of Lianjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tao was a native of Lianjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父震公，家縣東岱堡，海寇破岱堡，張氏殲焉。

translations.literal: His father Zhengong's family lived at Dongdai Fort east of the county; sea bandits destroyed Dongdai Fort and the Zhang clan was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhengong's family lived at Dongdai Fort east of the county. Sea bandits destroyed the fort and wiped out the Zhang clan.

sentences.zh: 震公適他往，獨免。

translations.literal: Zhengong happened to be away and alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengong happened to be away and alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 燾方七歲，為所掠，轉徙傭於清漳。

translations.literal: Tao was then seven; he was captured and eventually passed from place to place, hired out as a servant in Qingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was then seven. He was captured and eventually passed from place to place, hired out as a servant in Qingzhang.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，燾年二十餘矣，時時念父母。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi, Tao was over twenty and often thought of his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kangxi, Tao was over twenty and often thought of his parents.

sentences.zh: 顧被掠時幼，不審鄉縣，以人謂其語音似連江，而追憶父似名天貞，乃走還連江，數日無所鄉。

translations.literal: But when he was taken he was young and did not know his home county; because people said his accent sounded like Lianjiang, and recalling that his father's name seemed to be Tianzhen, he ran back to Lianjiang, yet for days found nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: But he had been taken when young and did not know his home county. Because people said his accent sounded like Lianjiang, and recalling that his father's name seemed to be Tianzhen, he ran back to Lianjiang, yet for days found nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 或問何為，以張天貞問。

translations.literal: When someone asked what he wanted, he inquired after Zhang Tianzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked what he wanted, he inquired after Zhang Tianzhen.

sentences.zh: 震公聞之，曰：「天貞，吾亡弟，彼焉識之？

translations.literal: Zhengong heard of it and said, "Tianzhen is my deceased younger brother—how would he know him?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhengong heard of it and said, "Tianzhen is my deceased younger brother—how would he know him?"

sentences.zh: 」走視問其詳，喜挾以歸，使見母。

translations.literal: He ran to see him and ask the details, rejoiced, and took him home, presenting him to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He ran to see him and ask for details, rejoiced, and took him home to present him to his mother.

sentences.zh: 燾追憶母容貌，曰：「非吾母也。

translations.literal: Tao, recalling his mother's appearance, said, "This is not my mother."
translations.idiomatic: Tao, recalling his mother's appearance, said, "This is not my mother."

sentences.zh: 」震公曰：「汝母已死於賊，此汝後母耳。

translations.literal: Zhengong said, "Your mother died at the hands of the bandits; this is your stepmother."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengong said, "Your mother died at the hands of the bandits; this is your stepmother."

sentences.zh: 」燾大慟，為母補行喪服三年，而事後母如母。

translations.literal: Tao grieved bitterly, observed three years of mourning for his mother in absentia, and served his stepmother as he would his own mother.
translations.idiomatic: Tao grieved bitterly, observed three years of mourning for his mother in absentia, and served his stepmother as he would his own mother.

sentences.zh: 硃壽命，江西餘干人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouming, a native of Yugan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouming was a native of Yugan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，遇寇，與母李相失，壽命日夜泣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when bandits came, he lost contact with his mother Li; Shouming wept day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when bandits came, he lost contact with his mother Li, and Shouming wept day and night.

sentences.zh: 既，聞母為禁旅所俘，屬正藍旗。

translations.literal: Later he heard his mother had been captured by the Banner garrison and belonged to the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he heard his mother had been captured by the Banner garrison and assigned to the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 壽命徒步走京師，乞於市，忍飢積錢將贖母。

translations.literal: Shouming walked to the capital, begged in the markets, endured hunger, and saved money to redeem his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shouming walked to the capital, begged in the markets, endured hunger, and saved money to redeem his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之得母所在，而主者邀重購，拒壽命。

translations.literal: After a long time he found where his mother was, but her master demanded a high price and refused Shouming.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he found where his mother was, but her master demanded a high price and refused to release her to Shouming.

sentences.zh: 壽命日跽其門外，膝為痺。

translations.literal: Shouming knelt daily at his gate until his knees grew numb.
translations.idiomatic: Shouming knelt daily at his gate until his knees grew numb.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士邵遠平高其行，為捐金以贖，暫留遠平家。

translations.literal: Reader-in-waiting Shao Yuanping admired his conduct and donated money to redeem her; for a time they stayed at Shao's home.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-waiting Shao Yuanping admired his conduct and donated money to redeem her. For a time they stayed at Shao's home.

sentences.zh: 母卞，小不當意輒詬罵，或捽而批其頰，壽命益嬉笑。

translations.literal: His mother was hot-tempered; the least displeasure brought scolding, and sometimes she would seize him and slap his cheeks, yet Shouming only smiled all the more.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was hot-tempered; the least displeasure brought scolding, and sometimes she would seize him and slap his cheeks, yet Shouming only smiled all the more.

sentences.zh: 居數月，附舟還。

translations.literal: After several months they took passage on a boat and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After several months they took passage on a boat and returned home.

sentences.zh: 壽命不知書，語質，每言：「在母腹日敢母血三合，那忍不報？

translations.literal: Shouming could not read; his speech was plain. He often said, "In my mother's womb I took three he of her blood each day—how could I bear not to repay her?"
translations.idiomatic: Shouming could not read, and his speech was plain. He often said, "In my mother's womb I took three he of her blood each day—how could I bear not to repay her?"

sentences.zh: 潘天成，字錫疇，江南溧陽人。

translations.literal: Pan Tiancheng, styled Xichou, a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tiancheng, styled Xichou, was a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遇家難，父母挈子女出避仇。

translations.literal: At thirteen he met with family disaster; his parents took the children and fled to escape enemies.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he met with family disaster. His parents took the children and fled to escape their enemies.

sentences.zh: 天成行後，幾為仇所斃。

translations.literal: Tiancheng walked behind and was nearly killed by their enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng walked behind and was nearly killed by their enemies.

sentences.zh: 既得免，乃行求父母。

translations.literal: Once he had escaped, he set out to seek his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had escaped, he set out to seek his parents.

sentences.zh: 經青陽白沙廟，宿廢廟，聞虎聲，為詩述悲。

translations.literal: Passing Bai Sha Temple in Qingyang, he lodged in a ruined temple, heard tigers, and composed a poem expressing his grief.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Bai Sha Temple in Qingyang, he lodged in a ruined temple, heard tigers, and composed a poem expressing his grief.

sentences.zh: 往來徽州、寧國所屬州縣，跡父母所在，至則又他徙。

translations.literal: He traveled back and forth among the prefectures and counties subordinate to Huizhou and Ningguo, tracking where his parents might be, but whenever he reached a place they had already moved elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled back and forth among the prefectures and counties under Huizhou and Ningguo, tracking his parents, but whenever he reached a place they had already moved on.

sentences.zh: 天成行經村聚，輒播{兆鼓}作鄉語大呼。

translations.literal: Whenever Tiancheng passed through a village, he would beat a drum and shout loudly in the local dialect.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tiancheng passed through a village, he would beat a drum and shout loudly in the local dialect.

sentences.zh: 至江西界，母金自巷出，就問之，始相識。

translations.literal: Reaching the Jiangxi border, his mother Jin came out from an alley to question him, and only then did they recognize each other.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the Jiangxi border, his mother Jin came out from an alley to question him, and only then did they recognize each other.

sentences.zh: 乃得父及其弟、妹，皆無恙。

translations.literal: He then found his father and his younger brother and sister, all unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: He then found his father and his younger brother and sister, all unharmed.

sentences.zh: 時天成年十五，欲歸苦無貲，出行貸。

translations.literal: Tiancheng was then fifteen; he wished to return home but had no funds, so he went out to borrow money.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng was then fifteen. He wished to return home but had no funds, so he went out to borrow money.

sentences.zh: 又六年，使其弟從父歸，天成奉母挈妹以行。

translations.literal: Six years later he sent his younger brother home with their father; Tiancheng escorted his mother and took his sister along.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he sent his younger brother home with their father while Tiancheng escorted his mother and took his sister along.

sentences.zh: 遇風雪，負母行數里，還抱妹，往復跣行，足流血，入雪盡殷。

translations.literal: They met wind and snow; he carried his mother for several li, then returned for his sister, going back and forth barefoot until his feet bled and the snow where he walked was stained red.
translations.idiomatic: They met wind and snow. He carried his mother for several li, then returned for his sister, going back and forth barefoot until his feet bled and the snow where he walked was stained red.

sentences.zh: 既歸，出行販以養，暇則讀書。

translations.literal: After returning home, he went out peddling to support the family and read books in his spare time.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he peddled goods to support the family and read books in his spare time.

sentences.zh: 荊溪湯之錡出高攀龍門，治性理之學，賢天成，天成從受業焉。

translations.literal: Tang Zhiqi of Jingxi was a disciple of Gao Panlong and devoted himself to Neo-Confucian moral philosophy; he esteemed Tiancheng, and Tiancheng studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhiqi of Jingxi was a disciple of Gao Panlong and devoted himself to Neo-Confucian moral philosophy. He esteemed Tiancheng, and Tiancheng studied under him.

sentences.zh: 同縣許國昌遇天成尤厚，使為童子師。

translations.literal: Xu Guochang of the same county treated Tiancheng with particular kindness and had him serve as a tutor for boys.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guochang of the same county treated Tiancheng with particular kindness and employed him as a tutor for boys.

sentences.zh: 鄰家兒詈母，天成召其鄉老人呼兒共懲之，兒悔謝乃巳。

translations.literal: A neighbor's child cursed his mother; Tiancheng summoned the village elders to call the child and jointly punish him; the child repented and apologized, and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's child cursed his mother, Tiancheng summoned the village elders to call the child and jointly punish him. The child repented and apologized, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 及父母卒，遊學桐城，遂隸籍為安慶府學生。

translations.literal: After his parents died, he went to study in Tongcheng and was enrolled as a student of Anqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he went to study in Tongcheng and was enrolled as a student of Anqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居二十餘年，移家江寧，天成學益進，狷潔不以乾當道。

translations.literal: He lived there more than twenty years, then moved his family to Jiangning; Tiancheng's learning advanced further, and he was upright and pure, never seeking favor from the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He lived there more than twenty years, then moved his family to Jiangning. Tiancheng's learning advanced further, and he was upright and pure, never seeking favor from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 終窮餓，年七十四卒，葬惠應寺側。

translations.literal: He ended in poverty and hunger, dying at seventy-four, and was buried beside Huiying Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He ended in poverty and hunger, dying at seventy-four, and was buried beside Huiying Temple.

sentences.zh: 國昌子重炎，師天成，編刻其遺書為鐵廬集。

translations.literal: Guochang's son Chongyan studied under Tiancheng and edited and published his posthumous writings as the Tielu Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang's son Chongyan studied under Tiancheng and edited and published his posthumous writings as the Tielu Collection.

sentences.zh: 翁運槐，字楫山；

translations.literal: Weng Yunhuai, styled Jishan;
translations.idiomatic: Weng Yunhuai, styled Jishan;

sentences.zh: 運標，字晉公：浙江餘姚人。

translations.literal: Yunbiao, styled Jingong: natives of Yuyao in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yunbiao, styled Jingong: natives of Yuyao in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父瀛，往廣西，道湖南。

translations.literal: Their father Ying was traveling to Guangxi by way of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Ying was traveling to Guangxi by way of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 一夕，泊舟祁陽新塘，失所在，舟人求不得，還報，歸其行篋，鎖在而鑰亡。

translations.literal: One night he moored his boat at Xintang in Qiyang and disappeared; the boatmen searched but could not find him and returned to report; they sent back his traveling case—the lock was still on it but the key was gone.
translations.idiomatic: One night he moored his boat at Xintang in Qiyang and disappeared. The boatmen searched but could not find him and returned to report. They sent back his traveling case—the lock was still on it but the key was gone.

sentences.zh: 時運槐、運標皆幼，運槐年十三，行求父不得，以病歸。

translations.literal: Yunhuai and Yunbiao were both young then; Yunhuai was thirteen, set out to seek his father but could not find him, and returned home ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yunhuai and Yunbiao were both young then. Yunhuai was thirteen when he set out to seek his father but could not find him, and returned home ill.

sentences.zh: 運標，雍正元年成進士，與運槐复求父，遍湖南境，更二年不得。

translations.literal: Yunbiao passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Yongzheng and, together with Yunhuai, again sought their father, searching throughout Hunan; after two more years they still could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunbiao passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Yongzheng and, together with Yunhuai, again sought their father throughout Hunan. After two more years they still could not find him.

sentences.zh: 一夕，复泊新塘，遇土人鄭海還，言距今三十年，弟海生墮水，格敗葦不死。

translations.literal: One night they again moored at Xintang and met the local man Zheng Haihuan, who said that thirty years ago his younger brother Haisheng fell into the water and, clinging to broken reeds, did not drown.
translations.idiomatic: One night they again moored at Xintang and met the local man Zheng Haihuan, who said that thirty years ago his younger brother Haisheng fell into the water and, clinging to broken reeds, did not drown.

sentences.zh: 視葦間有屍，因瘞之白沙洲，身有鑰在囊，藏為識。

translations.literal: Seeing a corpse among the reeds, he buried it on Baisha Zhou; there was a key in a pouch on the body, which he kept as a token.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a corpse among the reeds, he buried it on Baisha Zhou. There was a key in a pouch on the body, which he kept as a token.

sentences.zh: 乃遣力以囊鑰還，鑰與行篋鎖牝牡合，囊則運槐女兄昔年制以奉父者也。

translations.literal: They sent men to return the pouch and key; the key matched the lock on the traveling case, male and female parts fitting together, and the pouch was one Yunhuai's elder sister had made years before to present to their father.
translations.idiomatic: They sent men to return the pouch and key. The key matched the lock on the traveling case, and the pouch was one Yunhuai's elder sister had made years before to present to their father.

sentences.zh: 乃痛哭啟攢，以父喪還葬，而於瘞處留封樹焉，時雍正五年八月也。

translations.literal: They then wept bitterly, opened the burial, and brought their father's remains home for burial, while leaving a mound and trees at the original burial site—it was the eighth month of the fifth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: They then wept bitterly, opened the burial, and brought their father's remains home for reburial, while leaving a mound and trees at the original site. It was the eighth month of the fifth year of Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 運標謁選，得湖南武陵知縣。

translations.literal: Yunbiao went to await appointment and was assigned magistrate of Wuling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunbiao went to await appointment and was assigned magistrate of Wuling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 嘗有兄弟爭田訟，運標方詣勘，忽掩涕。

translations.literal: Once two brothers were litigating over farmland; Yunbiao had just gone to inspect the site when he suddenly covered his face and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Once two brothers were litigating over farmland. Yunbiao had just gone to inspect the site when he suddenly covered his face and wept.

sentences.zh: 訟者請其故，曰：「吾兄弟日相依，及官此，與吾兄別。

translations.literal: The litigants asked why; he said, "My brother and I depended on each other day by day, but when I took this office I parted from my elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: The litigants asked why. He said, "My brother and I depended on each other day by day, but when I took this office I parted from my elder brother."

sentences.zh: 今見汝兄弟，思吾兄，故悲耳。

translations.literal: Now seeing you brothers, I think of my elder brother, and so I grieve."
translations.idiomatic: Now seeing you brothers, I think of my elder brother, and so I grieve."

sentences.zh: 」訟者為感泣罷訟。

translations.literal: The litigants were moved to tears and dropped their lawsuit.
translations.idiomatic: The litigants were moved to tears and dropped their lawsuit.

sentences.zh: 縣東堤圮，水虐民，縣又無書院，運標為修築，民以運標姓名其堤與書院。

translations.literal: The eastern dike of the county collapsed and flood waters afflicted the people; the county also had no academy. Yunbiao had them repaired, and the people named the dike and the academy after Yunbiao.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern dike of the county collapsed and flood waters afflicted the people, and the county had no academy. Yunbiao had them repaired, and the people named the dike and the academy after him.

sentences.zh: 擢道州知州，縣通

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Daozhou; the counties connected
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Daozhou; the counties connected

sentences.zh: 郴、桂，鑿山八十餘里為坦道。

translations.literal: Chen and Gui, and he cut through the mountains for more than eighty li to make a level road.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Gui, and he cut through the mountains for more than eighty li to make a level road.

sentences.zh: 疫，親持方藥巡視，曰：「我民父母，子弟病，奈何不一顧耶？

translations.literal: When epidemic struck, he personally carried medicines on his rounds and said, "I am father and mother to my people—when sons and younger brothers fall ill, how can I fail to look in on them?"
translations.idiomatic: When epidemic struck, he personally carried medicines on his rounds and said, "I am father and mother to my people—when sons and younger brothers fall ill, how can I fail to look in on them?"

sentences.zh: 」年六十，卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 運標知武陵，建祠白沙洲，起鑰亭，買田，俾鄭氏世董之。

translations.literal: When Yunbiao served as magistrate of Wuling, he built a shrine at Baisha Zhou, erected a Key Pavilion, purchased land, and had the Zheng clan supervise it in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Wuling, Yunbiao built a shrine at Baisha Zhou, erected a Key Pavilion, purchased land, and entrusted the Zheng clan with its perpetual supervision.

sentences.zh: 知道州，拜祠下，哀感行路。

translations.literal: When he served as prefect of Daozhou, he bowed at the shrine, and his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as prefect of Daozhou, he bowed at the shrine, and his grief moved all who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 楊士選，字有貞，江南吳縣人。

translations.literal: Yang Shixuan, styled Youzhen, a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shixuan, styled Youzhen, was a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 方六歲，入塾，塾師為說古人孝行，輒窮其本末，歸告父母：「兒他日亦當如是。

translations.literal: When he was six he entered school; when the schoolmaster told stories of ancient filial conduct, he would press for every detail, and returning home would tell his parents, "I too shall be like this someday."
translations.idiomatic: When he was six he entered school. Whenever the schoolmaster told stories of ancient filial conduct, he pressed for every detail and, returning home, told his parents, "I too shall be like this someday."

sentences.zh: 」父商於河南。

translations.literal: His father was doing business in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father was doing business in Henan.

sentences.zh: 喪貲而病。

translations.literal: He lost his capital and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his capital and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 士選年十六，往省，渡河風雨，士選泣禱得不覆，人稱「孝子舟」，奉其父還裡。

translations.literal: Shixuan was sixteen when he went to visit him. Crossing the river in wind and rain, Shixuan wept and prayed that the boat would not capsize; people called it the "Filial Son's Boat," and he brought his father home.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan was sixteen when he went to visit him. Crossing the river in wind and rain, Shixuan wept and prayed that the boat would not capsize. People called it the "Filial Son's Boat," and he brought his father home.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，士選與妻唐食糠籺，共營甘旨奉父母。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, Shixuan and his wife Tang ate bran cakes while together preparing delicacies to serve their parents.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine, Shixuan and his wife Tang ate bran cakes while together preparing delicacies for their parents.

sentences.zh: 居喪營葬，身穿負土，唐為姑吮疽。

translations.literal: During mourning and burial arrangements, he wore hemp and carried earth on his shoulders; Tang sucked the pus from a carbuncle on her mother-in-law's body.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning and burial arrangements, he wore hemp mourning garb and carried earth on his shoulders, while Tang sucked the pus from a carbuncle on her mother-in-law's body.

sentences.zh: 徐大中，湖北潛山人。

translations.literal: Xu Dazhong, a native of Qianshan in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dazhong was a native of Qianshan in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 潛山俗重風水，大中喪母，厝棺居室傍未葬。

translations.literal: Qianshan custom valued geomancy; when Dazhong's mother died, he placed the coffin beside the house and did not bury her.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan custom valued geomancy. When Dazhong's mother died, he placed the coffin beside the house and did not bury her.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十七年，縣大水，齧前和，失其屍，大中大慟。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong, a great flood struck the county, eroded the front embankment, and lost the corpse; Dazhong grieved bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong, a great flood struck the county, eroded the front embankment, and swept away the corpse. Dazhong grieved bitterly.

sentences.zh: 水初退，求屍於沙中，得一足，襪敗猶未盡，色餘黃，其母斂時裝也。

translations.literal: When the water first receded, he searched for the corpse in the sand and found a foot; the sock though torn was not entirely gone, and the color still showed yellow—it was what his mother had worn at encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: When the water first receded, he searched for the corpse in the sand and found a foot. The sock, though torn, was not entirely gone, and the color still showed yellow—it was what his mother had worn at encoffining.

sentences.zh: 大中抱足泣，路人見者語曰：「去此二里許，樹上懸屍，濕綿裹，缺一足。

translations.literal: Dazhong embraced the foot and wept. A passerby who saw him said, "About two li from here a corpse hangs in a tree, wrapped in wet cotton, missing one foot."
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong embraced the foot and wept. A passerby who saw him said, "About two li from here a corpse hangs in a tree, wrapped in wet cotton, missing one foot."

sentences.zh: 」奔視良是，但脫頤下骨，負歸改斂。

translations.literal: He ran to look and it was indeed so, but the jawbone had come off; he carried it home and re-encoffined her.
translations.idiomatic: He ran to look and it was indeed so, but the jawbone had come off. He carried the remains home and re-encoffined her.

sentences.zh: 忽有人若丐入其家，曰：「吾拾得頤下骨。

translations.literal: Suddenly a man like a beggar entered his home and said, "I picked up the jawbone."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a man like a beggar entered his home and said, "I picked up the jawbone."

sentences.zh: 」​​取與合，人傳為異。

translations.literal: He brought it and they joined it together; people spread word of it as a marvel.
translations.idiomatic: He brought it and they joined it together. People spread word of it as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 學官欲上其事，大中曰：「我久不葬母，乃遘此禍，我天地間一罪人耳。

translations.literal: The school official wished to report the matter upward; Dazhong said, "I long failed to bury my mother and thus met this disaster—I am nothing but a sinner between heaven and earth."
translations.idiomatic: The school official wished to report the matter upward, but Dazhong said, "I long failed to bury my mother and thus met this disaster—I am nothing but a sinner between heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 舉我孝，於及時葬親者謂何也？

translations.literal: To hold me up as filial—what would that say to those who bury their parents in timely fashion?"
translations.idiomatic: To hold me up as filial—what would that say to those who bury their parents in timely fashion?"

sentences.zh: 」堅卻之。

translations.literal: He firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 沈仁業，字振先，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Shen Renye, styled Zhenxian, a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Renye, styled Zhenxian, was a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父賈於安南，娶婦生子女，仁業八歲從父歸，而母為外國女，例不得入中國，不能從。

translations.literal: His father traded in Annam, married, and had children; Renye at eight returned with his father, but his mother was a foreign woman and by regulation could not enter China, so she could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: His father traded in Annam, married, and had children. Renye returned with his father at eight, but his mother was a foreign woman and by regulation could not enter China, so she could not follow.

sentences.zh: 仁業長而思母，父卒，乃圖父像，渡海省母。

translations.literal: When Renye grew up he thought of his mother; after his father died he painted his father's portrait and crossed the sea to visit his mother.
