translations.idiomatic: When Renye grew up he longed for his mother. After his father died he painted his father's portrait and crossed the sea to visit her.

sentences.zh: 安南有兵事，母挾幼子女竄山谷中，仁業行求得之，不食七日矣。

translations.literal: There was warfare in Annam; his mother fled into the mountains with her young children; Renye traveled and found them—they had not eaten for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: There was warfare in Annam. His mother fled into the mountains with her young children. Renye traveled and found them—they had not eaten for seven days.

sentences.zh: 居二年，有義其行者為具舟，舟入海，颶作，觸海中山。

translations.literal: After two years there, someone who admired his conduct provided a boat; the boat entered the sea, a hurricane arose, and it struck a mountain in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: After two years there, someone who admired his conduct provided a boat. The boat entered the sea, a hurricane arose, and it struck a mountain in the sea.

sentences.zh: 仁業抱母泣，風轉，挾母過山至瓊州。

translations.literal: Renye embraced his mother and wept; the wind shifted and carried them past the mountain to Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renye embraced his mother and wept. The wind shifted and carried them past the mountain to Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 吏執例拒仁業母不得入，仁業涕泗請，莫應。

translations.literal: Officials invoked the regulations and refused to allow Renye's mother entry; Renye pleaded with tears but got no response.
translations.idiomatic: Officials invoked the regulations and refused to allow Renye's mother entry. Renye pleaded with tears but got no response.

sentences.zh: 久之，有老吏謂康熙間有故事，檢文書得之，仁業乃奉母及弟妹以歸。

translations.literal: After a long time an old clerk said there was a precedent from the Kangxi reign; they searched the documents and found it, and Renye then brought his mother and younger siblings home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time an old clerk said there was a precedent from the Kangxi reign. They searched the documents and found it, and Renye then brought his mother and younger siblings home.

sentences.zh: 魏樹德，陝西蒲城人。

translations.literal: Wei Shude, a native of Pucheng in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shude was a native of Pucheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父季龍，出佐幕客遊，樹德猶在娠。

translations.literal: His father Jilong went out as an aide on a tour and Shude was still in the womb.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jilong went out as an aide on a tour while Shude was still in the womb.

sentences.zh: 幼劬學，母力針黹以活。

translations.literal: From youth he studied diligently; his mother worked needlework to support them.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied diligently while his mother worked needlework to support them.

sentences.zh: 季龍久不歸，樹德以嘉慶十五年舉於鄉，乃行求父。

translations.literal: Jilong long did not return; Shude passed the provincial examination in the fifteenth year of Jiaqing and then set out to seek his father.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong long did not return. Shude passed the provincial examination in the fifteenth year of Jiaqing and then set out to seek his father.

sentences.zh: 初聞季龍自福建轉客廣東，先詣福建，求不得，乃詣廣東，遇知季龍者，為約略言葬處，遍求之，得志石荒塚中，乃持喪還。

translations.literal: At first he heard Jilong had moved from Fujian to Guangdong; he first went to Fujian but could not find him, then went to Guangdong, met someone who knew Jilong, who roughly indicated the burial place; searching everywhere he found the epitaph stone in a desolate tomb and brought the remains home.
translations.idiomatic: At first he heard Jilong had moved from Fujian to Guangdong. He first went to Fujian but could not find him, then went to Guangdong and met someone who knew Jilong, who roughly indicated the burial place. Searching everywhere, he found the epitaph stone in a desolate tomb and brought the remains home.

sentences.zh: 逾年，母卒，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: The next year his mother died; he lived by the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his mother died, and he lived by the tomb for three years.

sentences.zh: 除高陵訓導，求呂柟遺書，授諸生。

translations.literal: He was appointed instructor at Gaoling, sought out Lü Nan's posthumous writings, and taught the students.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed instructor at Gaoling, sought out Lü Nan's posthumous writings, and taught the students.

sentences.zh: 久之，以老乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested retirement on account of age and died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he requested retirement on account of age and died.

sentences.zh: 李汝恢，江西廬陵人。

translations.literal: Li Ruhui, a native of Luling in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruhui was a native of Luling in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 父仲鴻，業醫，遊無方。

translations.literal: His father Zhonghong practiced medicine and wandered without fixed destination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhonghong practiced medicine and wandered without fixed destination.

sentences.zh: 汝恢年十三，出求父。

translations.literal: Ruhui at thirteen set out to seek his father.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Ruhui set out to seek his father.

sentences.zh: 初至四川，又至廣東，皆未遇。

translations.literal: He first reached Sichuan, then Guangdong, but did not find him in either place.
translations.idiomatic: He first reached Sichuan, then Guangdong, but did not find him in either place.

sentences.zh: 乃節日用得百金，復出，遍涉江湖，遇仲鴻貴築。

translations.literal: He then economized day by day until he had a hundred taels of gold, set out again, traveled throughout the Yangtze region, and found Zhonghong at Guizhu.
translations.idiomatic: He then economized day by day until he had a hundred taels of gold, set out again, traveled throughout the Yangtze region, and found Zhonghong at Guizhu.

sentences.zh: 仲鴻有弟亦出遊，既歸，日念弟。

translations.literal: Zhonghong had a younger brother who had also gone traveling; after returning home he daily thought of his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghong had a younger brother who had also gone traveling. After returning home he daily thought of his brother.

sentences.zh: 汝恢乃更出求其從父，得諸柳州。

translations.literal: Ruhui then set out again to seek his uncle and found him at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui then set out again to seek his uncle and found him at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲鴻乃樂甚，遽無疾而卒，汝恢喪葬盡禮。

translations.literal: Zhonghong was overjoyed, then suddenly died without illness; Ruhui observed the funeral rites in full.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghong was overjoyed, then suddenly died without illness. Ruhui observed the funeral rites in full.

sentences.zh: 母痺，奉事尤謹。

translations.literal: His mother had paralysis; he served her with particular care.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had paralysis, and he served her with particular care.

sentences.zh: 鄭立本，江蘇蕭縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Liben, a native of Xiao County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Liben was a native of Xiao County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父相德，坐罪戍新疆，立本方四歲。

translations.literal: His father Xiangde was sentenced to garrison duty in Xinjiang; Liben was then four.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiangde was sentenced to garrison duty in Xinjiang when Liben was four.

sentences.zh: 年十八，辭母以求父，母哭而誡之曰：「汝父左手小指缺一節，中有橫紋，幸相值，以此為驗。

translations.literal: At eighteen he took leave of his mother to seek his father; his mother wept and admonished him, "Your father's left little finger is missing a joint, with a horizontal ridge on it—if you happen to meet him, use this as proof."
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he took leave of his mother to seek his father. His mother wept and admonished him, "Your father's left little finger is missing a joint, with a horizontal ridge on it—if you happen to meet him, use this as proof."

sentences.zh: 」立本貧無貲，乞且行，至庫車。

translations.literal: Liben was poor and had no funds; he begged as he traveled and reached Kuche.
translations.idiomatic: Liben was poor and had no funds. He begged as he traveled and reached Kuche.

sentences.zh: 聞父戍綏來，綏來至庫車，三千餘裡，張格爾亂未定，官道塞，乃裡糧求路，獨行迷失道，還庫車。

translations.literal: He heard his father was garrisoned at Suilai; Suilai was over three thousand li from Kuche; Jahangir's rebellion was not yet settled and the official roads were blocked, so he carried provisions and sought a route, traveling alone, lost his way, and returned to Kuche.
translations.idiomatic: He heard his father was garrisoned at Suilai, over three thousand li from Kuche. Jahangir's rebellion was not yet settled and the official roads were blocked, so he carried provisions and sought a route, traveling alone. He lost his way and returned to Kuche.

sentences.zh: 待亂定，乃行至綏來，則父歿已數年。

translations.literal: Waiting until the rebellion was settled, he then traveled to Suilai, but his father had died several years before.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting until the rebellion was settled, he then traveled to Suilai, but his father had died several years before.

sentences.zh: 相德在戍授同戍子弟讀，歿，弟子為治葬。

translations.literal: Xiangde while garrisoned taught the children of fellow exiles to read; when he died his students arranged his burial.
translations.idiomatic: While garrisoned, Xiangde taught the children of fellow exiles to read. When he died his students arranged his burial.

sentences.zh: 立本哭墓而病，居二年，相德弟子力護視，故得不死。

translations.literal: Liben wept at the grave and fell ill; he stayed two years, and Xiangde's students strenuously watched over him, so he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Liben wept at the grave and fell ill. He stayed two years, and Xiangde's students strenuously watched over him, so he did not die.

sentences.zh: 病起，啟父瘞，體久化，左手獨存小指，缺一節，有橫紋，如母言。

translations.literal: When he recovered he opened his father's reburial site; the body had long since decomposed, but the left hand alone remained with the little finger missing a joint and bearing a horizontal ridge, just as his mother had said.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered he opened his father's reburial site. The body had long since decomposed, but the left hand alone remained with the little finger missing a joint and bearing a horizontal ridge, just as his mother had said.

sentences.zh: 立本駭慟，聞其事者皆嘆異，乃負骨歸葬，往還凡八年。

translations.literal: Liben was shocked and grieved; all who heard were amazed; he carried the bones home for burial—the round trip took eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Liben was shocked and grieved, and all who heard were amazed. He carried the bones home for burial—the round trip took eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 同治中，大學士曾國籓駐軍徐州，聞立本事，招往見，立本舉孟子召役往，召見不往語，謝不往見。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi reign, Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan was stationed with troops at Xuzhou; hearing of Liben's story he summoned him for an audience; Liben cited Mencius—"If called for labor one goes; if called for an audience one does not go"—and declined the summons.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi reign, Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan was stationed with troops at Xuzhou. Hearing of Liben's story he summoned him for an audience, but Liben cited Mencius—"If called for labor one goes; if called for an audience one does not go"—and declined.

sentences.zh: 國籓高其義，檄知縣以時存問。

translations.literal: Guofan admired his integrity and instructed the county magistrate to visit him regularly.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan admired his integrity and instructed the county magistrate to visit him regularly.

sentences.zh: 李學侗，山西介休人。

translations.literal: Li Xuetong, a native of Jiexiu in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuetong was a native of Jiexiu in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 生廷儀，道光中客死貴州荔波縣，有同行者斂而葬焉。

translations.literal: His father Tingyi died abroad in Libo County, Guizhou, during the Daoguang reign; a fellow traveler encoffined and buried him there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingyi died abroad in Libo County, Guizhou, during the Daoguang reign. A fellow traveler encoffined and buried him there.

sentences.zh: 學侗志欲歸父喪，貧，客授十餘年，積數百金，始克行。

translations.literal: Xuetong resolved to bring his father's remains home; poor, he tutored away from home for more than ten years and saved several hundred taels before he could set out.
translations.idiomatic: Xuetong resolved to bring his father's remains home. Poor, he tutored away from home for more than ten years and saved several hundred taels before he could set out.

sentences.zh: 詣荔波，時方亂，貴州境亦騷動，屢遇險，乃達。

translations.literal: He went to Libo when there was turmoil; Guizhou territory was also in unrest; he met danger repeatedly before reaching his destination.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Libo when turmoil was abroad. Guizhou territory was also in unrest, and he met danger repeatedly before reaching his destination.

sentences.zh: 廷儀葬社稷壇山下，或以為先農壇，語廷儀同行者音轉，又以為西龍塘。

translations.literal: Tingyi was buried below the Altars of Soil and Grain; some thought it was the Altar of the First Farmer; the fellow traveler's speech turned the sound, and it was also taken to be Xilongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyi was buried below the Altars of Soil and Grain. Some thought it was the Altar of the First Farmer; the fellow traveler's speech turned the sound, and it was also taken to be Xilongtang.

sentences.zh: 學侗至，求西龍塘，無其地。

translations.literal: When Xuetong arrived he sought Xilongtang but found no such place.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuetong arrived he sought Xilongtang but found no such place.

sentences.zh: 慟哭周行諸叢塚，乃於社稷壇得焉。

translations.literal: Weeping bitterly he walked among the clustered tombs and finally found it at the Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping bitterly, he walked among the clustered tombs and finally found it at the Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 學侗持喪還葬，族人有客死而旅殯者，並載以歸。

translations.literal: Xuetong brought the remains home for burial; a clansman who had died abroad with only a temporary burial was also carried back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuetong brought the remains home for burial, and also carried back a clansman who had died abroad with only a temporary burial.

sentences.zh: 既葬，日必往視，持盂飯以祭。

translations.literal: After burial he went daily to visit, bringing a bowl of rice as an offering.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he went daily to visit, bringing a bowl of rice as an offering.

sentences.zh: 晚治易，有所撰述。

translations.literal: In his later years he studied the Changes and left written works.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he studied the Changes and left written works.

sentences.zh: 董士元，直隸臨榆人。

translations.literal: Dong Shiyuan, a native of Linyu in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shiyuan was a native of Linyu in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父行健，嘉慶中出關，去三月而士元生，行健遂不歸。

translations.literal: His father Xingjian passed through the pass in the Jiaqing reign; three months after he left Shiyuan was born, and Xingjian never returned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingjian passed through the pass in the Jiaqing reign. Three months after he left, Shiyuan was born, and Xingjian never returned.

sentences.zh: 士元幼思父，六歲，嘗失所在，翼日得之關外二里店。

translations.literal: From youth Shiyuan thought of his father; at six he once disappeared, and the next day was found at Erli Shop outside the pass.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shiyuan thought of his father. At six he once disappeared, and the next day was found at Erli Shop outside the pass.

sentences.zh: 母問其故，涕泣言曰：「欲尋父也。

translations.literal: His mother asked why; weeping he said, "I wanted to seek my father."
translations.idiomatic: His mother asked why. Weeping, he said, "I wanted to seek my father."

sentences.zh: 」年十五，戚商於奉天，士元請於母，從之往，求父消息不能得。

translations.literal: At fifteen a relative was doing business in Fengtian; Shiyuan asked his mother's leave and went along, but could not obtain news of his father.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen a relative was doing business in Fengtian. Shiyuan asked his mother's leave and went along, but could not obtain news of his father.

sentences.zh: 越十餘年，至阿什河，有言十年前在三姓南淘淇，嘗遇臨榆人，董姓，今不知存亡。

translations.literal: More than ten years later, reaching the Ashi River, someone said that ten years before at Taogi south of Sanxing he had met a man from Linyu surnamed Dong, whose present fate was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later, reaching the Ashi River, someone said that ten years before at Taogi south of Sanxing he had met a man from Linyu surnamed Dong, whose present fate was unknown.

sentences.zh: 士元乃往淘淇，地僻，行失道，久之始得達。

translations.literal: Shiyuan then went to Taogi; the place was remote; he lost his way and only after a long time reached it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan then went to Taogi. The place was remote; he lost his way and only after a long time reached it.

sentences.zh: 舉父姓名里居問居人，有知者，曰：「是嘗漁於此，死數年矣。

translations.literal: He gave his father's name and native place and asked all who lived there; someone who knew said, "He used to fish here and died several years ago."
translations.idiomatic: He gave his father's name and native place and asked all who lived there. Someone who knew said, "He used to fish here and died several years ago."

sentences.zh: 」士元大慟，得藁葬地，發塚審視，齧指血滴入骨，函以歸。

translations.literal: Shiyuan grieved bitterly, found the straw burial place, opened the tomb and examined the remains, bit his finger and let blood drip on the bones, placed them in a casket and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan grieved bitterly, found the straw burial place, opened the tomb and examined the remains, bit his finger and let blood drip on the bones, placed them in a casket, and returned.

sentences.zh: 至奉天，乃具棺還葬。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengtian he prepared a coffin and brought the remains home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fengtian, he prepared a coffin and brought the remains home for burial.

sentences.zh: 居二十餘年，母歿，喪葬如禮。

translations.literal: He lived there more than twenty years; when his mother died he observed mourning and burial according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He lived there more than twenty years. When his mother died he observed mourning and burial according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 至光緒初卒。

translations.literal: He died in the early Guangxu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the early Guangxu reign.

sentences.zh: 李復新，湖北襄城人。

translations.literal: Li Fuxin, a native of Xiangcheng in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuxin was a native of Xiangcheng in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末歲饑，復新出糴於郾。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen there was famine; Fuxin went to buy grain at Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chongzhen there was famine. Fuxin went to buy grain at Yan.

sentences.zh: 土寇賈成倫劫殺其父際春，復新歸，痛甚，誓復仇。

translations.literal: The local bandit Jia Chenglun robbed and killed his father Jichun; Fuxin returned, grieved bitterly, and swore revenge.
translations.idiomatic: The local bandit Jia Chenglun robbed and killed his father Jichun. Fuxin returned, grieved bitterly, and swore revenge.

sentences.zh: 時方亂，法不行，而成倫悍甚，復新乃謬懦示無復仇意，成倫易之。

translations.literal: Times were chaotic and the law went unenforced; Chenglun was very fierce, so Fuxin falsely played the coward and showed no intent of revenge; Chenglun took him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Times were chaotic and the law went unenforced. Chenglun was very fierce, so Fuxin falsely played the coward and showed no intent of revenge. Chenglun took him lightly.

sentences.zh: 順治初，復新始告官，獄成，會赦，成倫得減死。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi Fuxin at last reported to the authorities; the case was concluded, but an amnesty intervened and Chenglun received commuted death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi Fuxin at last reported to the authorities. The case was concluded, but an amnesty intervened and Chenglun received commuted death.

sentences.zh: 吏監詣徒所，復新伏道旁，俟其至，舉大石擊之，死。

translations.literal: Officials escorted him to the place of exile; Fuxin lay in wait by the road, and when Chenglun arrived he lifted a great stone and struck him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Officials escorted Chenglun to the place of exile. Fuxin lay in wait by the road, and when Chenglun arrived he lifted a great stone and struck him dead.

sentences.zh: 詣縣請就刑，縣愍其孝，上府，請勿竟獄，且旌表其門。

translations.literal: He went to the county to submit to punishment; the county, moved by his filial devotion, reported upward and asked that the case not be pursued to completion and that his gate be honored with an official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the county to submit to punishment. The county, moved by his filial devotion, reported upward and asked that the case not be pursued to completion and that his gate be honored with an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 府駮議，謂成倫已遇赦減死，復新擅殺，當用殺人律坐罪。

translations.literal: The prefecture rejected the proposal, saying Chenglun had already received commuted death through amnesty, while Fuxin had killed on his own authority and should be punished under the statute for homicide.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture rejected the proposal, saying Chenglun had already received commuted death through amnesty, while Fuxin had killed on his own authority and should be punished under the statute for homicide.

sentences.zh: 縣有老掾复具牘上府曰：「禮言父母之仇，不共戴天。

translations.literal: An old clerk in the county again submitted a memorial to the prefecture saying, "The Rites say that the debt owed one's parents' enemy is so deep one cannot live under the same sky."
translations.idiomatic: An old clerk in the county again submitted a memorial to the prefecture saying, "The Rites say that the debt owed one's parents' enemy is so deep one cannot live under the same sky."

sentences.zh: 又言報仇者，書於士殺之無罪。

translations.literal: They also say that one who takes revenge, as recorded among gentlemen, commits no crime in killing."
translations.idiomatic: They also say that one who takes revenge, as recorded among gentlemen, commits no crime in killing."

sentences.zh: 赦罪者一時之仁，復仇者千古之義。

translations.literal: Amnesty is a momentary act of benevolence; revenge is an eternal principle of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is a momentary act of benevolence; revenge is an eternal principle of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 成倫之罪，可赦於朝廷，復新之仇，難寬於人子。

translations.literal: Chenglun's crime may be pardoned by the court, but Fuxin's debt as a son cannot lightly be waived.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglun's crime may be pardoned by the court, but Fuxin's debt as a son cannot lightly be waived.

sentences.zh: 成倫且欲原貸，復新不免極刑，平允之論，似不如是。

translations.literal: Chenglun was moreover to be spared, while Fuxin would not escape the severest penalty—is this what fair judgment would say?
translations.idiomatic: Chenglun was moreover to be spared, while Fuxin would not escape the severest penalty—is this what fair judgment would say?

sentences.zh: 復新父子何辜，並遭大戮？

translations.literal: What guilt had Fuxin and his father that both should suffer violent death?
translations.idiomatic: What guilt had Fuxin and his father that both should suffer violent death?

sentences.zh: 凡有人心，誰不哀矜！

translations.literal: Whoever has a human heart—who would not pity them!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever has a human heart would pity them!

sentences.zh: 宜貰以無罪，仍旌其孝。

translations.literal: He should be pardoned as innocent and still honored for his filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He should be pardoned as innocent and still honored for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 」府乃用縣議，表其門日「孝烈」。

translations.literal: The prefecture then adopted the county's view and honored his gate with the title "Filial and Heroic."
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture then adopted the county's view and honored his gate with the title "Filial and Heroic."

sentences.zh: 黨國虎，陝西富平人。

translations.literal: Dang Guohu, a native of Fuping in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Guohu was a native of Fuping in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明末，父兄為族子所殺，國虎方幼。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming his father and elder brother were killed by a clansman; Guohu was still young.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming his father and elder brother were killed by a clansman while Guohu was still young.

sentences.zh: 順治初，國虎稍長，誘族子於野，撾殺之，併其子，詣縣自首入獄。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, when Guohu had grown somewhat, he lured the clansman into the wild, beat him to death, killed his son as well, and went to the county to surrender himself and enter prison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, when Guohu had grown somewhat, he lured the clansman into the wild, beat him to death, killed his son as well, and went to the county to surrender himself and enter prison.

sentences.zh: 知縣郭傳芳將貸之，國虎念父兄仇已雪，遂自經獄中。

translations.literal: Magistrate Guo Chuanfang was about to release him on bail; Guo Hu, reflecting that his father and brother's revenge had been avenged, hanged himself in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Guo Chuanfang was about to release him on bail, but Guo Hu, reflecting that his father and brother's revenge had been avenged, hanged himself in prison.

sentences.zh: 唐時縣人梁悅复親仇，傳芳立孝義祠，首悅而配以國虎。

translations.literal: During the Tang, native Liang Yue avenged his parent; Chuanfang established a Temple of Filial Piety and Righteousness, with Yue first and Guo Hu paired with him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang, a native named Liang Yue avenged his parent. Chuanfang established a Temple of Filial Piety and Righteousness, placing Yue first and pairing Guo Hu with him.

sentences.zh: 嚴廷瓚，浙江烏程人。

translations.literal: Yan Tingzan, a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzan was a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父時敏。

translations.literal: His father was Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Shimin.

sentences.zh: 族子暘，以姑為明大學士溫體仁妻，怙餘勢，時敏嘗斥其非。

translations.literal: A clansman Yang, whose aunt was the wife of Ming Grand Secretary Wen Tiren, relied on residual influence; Shimin had once reproved him for wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman named Yang, whose aunt was the wife of the Ming Grand Secretary Wen Tiren, relied on his family's lingering influence. Shimin had once reproved him for wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 暘陽與出遊，擠墮水死。

translations.literal: Yang feigned friendliness and went out with him on an excursion, pushed him, and he fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang feigned friendliness and invited him out on an excursion, then pushed him so that he fell into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚稍長，聞父死狀，訟暘論斬。

translations.literal: When Tingzan grew somewhat older, learning the circumstances of his father's death, he sued Yang and sought the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzan grew older and learned how his father had died, he sued Yang and sought the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 暘賄上官反其獄，得脫，益肆。

translations.literal: Yang bribed superiors to reverse the case, escaped, and became still more reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Yang bribed his superiors to reverse the verdict, escaped, and became even more reckless.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚奉母避長興，買斧誓復仇。

translations.literal: Tingzan attended his mother and fled to Changxing, bought an axe, and swore to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzan cared for his mother and fled to Changxing, bought an axe, and swore to take revenge.

sentences.zh: 歲還裡省墓，遇暘，陽暱就之，暘以為畏己也。

translations.literal: Each year when he returned to his village to visit the graves, he encountered Yang; Yang feigned intimacy and approached him, thinking Tingzan feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Each year when he returned to his village to tend the graves, he encountered Yang, who feigned warmth and approached him, thinking Tingzan feared him.

sentences.zh: 母卒，以喪歸。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he returned for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he returned home for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 方村演劇，暘高坐以觀。

translations.literal: The village was staging a play, and Yang sat up high to watch.
translations.idiomatic: The village was staging a play, and Yang sat up high to watch.

sentences.zh: 廷瓚直前斧裂其首，斷項，詣縣自首。

translations.literal: Tingzan went straight up, split his head with an axe, severed his neck, and went to the county seat to surrender himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzan went straight up to him, split his head with an axe, severed his neck, and went to the county seat to surrender himself.

sentences.zh: 縣嘉其孝，欲生之，獄上，按察使將援韓愈復仇議為請，廷瓚遽死獄中，或曰暘家賄獄吏殺之。

translations.literal: The county praised his filial piety and wished to spare his life; the case went up, and the provincial surveillance commissioner was about to cite Han Yu's discourse on vengeance to plead on his behalf, when Tingzan suddenly died in prison — some said Yang's family bribed the jailer to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The county praised his filial piety and wished to spare his life. When the case went up, the provincial surveillance commissioner was about to cite Han Yu's discourse on vengeance on his behalf, but Tingzan suddenly died in prison. Some said Yang's family had bribed the jailer to kill him.

sentences.zh: 陸起鶤、起鵬，貴州安順人。

translations.literal: Lu Qikun and Qipeng, natives of Anshun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qikun and Qipeng were natives of Anshun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 父希武。

translations.literal: Their father was Xiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Their father was Xiwu.

sentences.zh: 明末水西安邦彥叛，破安順，陸氏舉室自焚，希武與起鵬幸得脫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, An Bangyan of Shuixi rebelled, broke Anshun, and the Lu household burned themselves to death; Xiwu and Qipeng fortunately escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming, An Bangyan of Shuixi rebelled and overran Anshun. The Lu household burned themselves to death, but Xiwu and Qipeng fortunately escaped.

sentences.zh: 起鶤自火中跳而出，遇賊，為所掠。

translations.literal: Qikun leaped out from the fire, encountered bandits, and was carried off by them.
translations.idiomatic: Qikun leaped out from the flames, encountered bandits, and was carried off by them.

sentences.zh: 居數月，賊攻貴陽，自間道出求父及弟，未得。

translations.literal: After several months, when the bandits attacked Guiyang, he slipped out by a secret route to seek his father and brother but did not find them.
translations.idiomatic: After several months, when the bandits attacked Guiyang, he slipped out by a secret route to search for his father and brother but could not find them.

sentences.zh: 順治初，師下安順，起鶤乃歸。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi reign, the army descended on Anshun and Qikun returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi reign, the imperial army descended on Anshun, and Qikun returned home.

sentences.zh: 诇知起鵬所在，鬻產贖以歸。

translations.literal: Learning where Qipeng was, he sold property to ransom him and bring him home.
translations.idiomatic: Learning where Qipeng was, he sold property to ransom him and bring him home.

sentences.zh: 起鵬具言父為邦彥黨羅戎所殺，被掠鬻入土司中。

translations.literal: Qipeng fully recounted that their father had been killed by Luo Rong, a follower of Bangyan, and that he had been captured and sold into a native chieftain's domain.
translations.idiomatic: Qipeng fully recounted that their father had been killed by Luo Rong, a follower of Bangyan, and that he himself had been captured and sold into a native chieftain's domain.

sentences.zh: 時戎已就撫，起鶤兄弟訴父前為戎殺事，下巡道，巡道判戎罰鍰。

translations.literal: By then Rong had submitted to pacification; the Qikun brothers sued over their father's earlier killing by Rong; the case went to the circuit intendant, who sentenced Rong to a fine.
translations.idiomatic: By then Rong had submitted to pacification. The Qikun brothers sued over their father's earlier killing by Rong. The case went to the circuit intendant, who sentenced Rong to pay a fine.

sentences.zh: 起鶤始不肯受，既而曰：「不受金，是使戎知吾必報也。

translations.literal: Qikun at first refused to accept it, then said: "If I do not accept the money, that will show Rong that I must surely take revenge."
translations.idiomatic: Qikun at first refused to accept the payment, then said, "If I do not accept the money, that will show Rong that I am bound to take revenge."

sentences.zh: 」乃受金，戎謂訟已決，不為備。

translations.literal: So he accepted the money; Rong thought the lawsuit was settled and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: So he accepted the money. Rong thought the lawsuit was settled and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 起鵬故善騎射，結壯士七，日夜伺戎隙。

translations.literal: Qipeng had been skilled at riding and archery; he gathered seven stalwart men and day and night watched for an opening against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Qipeng had been skilled at riding and archery. He gathered seven stalwart men and day and night watched for an opening against Rong.

sentences.zh: 一日，戎以事入安順，其徒皆從，起鶤、起鵬與七人者盟，挾弓弩伏城外，令所親醉戎。

translations.literal: One day Rong entered Anshun on business with all his followers; Qikun, Qipeng, and the seven men swore an oath, took bows and crossbows and lay in ambush outside the city, and had a confidant get Rong drunk.
translations.idiomatic: One day Rong entered Anshun on business with all his followers. Qikun, Qipeng, and the seven men swore an oath, took bows and crossbows, and lay in ambush outside the city while a confidant got Rong drunk.

sentences.zh: 戎既醉而出，起鵬射戎中肩，即前斫之，七人者皆起，盡縛其徒，得與戎同殺父者四人，剖心以祭父。

translations.literal: When Rong, already drunk, came out, Qipeng shot him in the shoulder, then rushed forward and hacked him; the seven men all rose, bound all his followers, found four who had joined Rong in killing their father, and cut out their hearts to sacrifice to their father.
translations.idiomatic: When the drunken Rong came out, Qipeng shot him in the shoulder and rushed forward to hack him down. The seven men rose together, bound all his followers, found four who had joined Rong in killing their father, and cut out their hearts to sacrifice to him.

sentences.zh: 起鶤令起鵬走避，戎黨訴巡道，起鶤赴質，抗辯不稍屈，巡道釋不問。

translations.literal: Qikun told Qipeng to flee and hide; Rong's faction sued to the circuit intendant; Qikun presented himself for questioning, argued without yielding in the least, and the intendant released him without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Qikun told Qipeng to flee and hide. When Rong's faction sued to the circuit intendant, Qikun presented himself for questioning, argued without yielding in the least, and the intendant released him without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 虞爾忘、爾雪，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Yu Erwang and Erxue, natives of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Erwang and Erxue were natives of Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 國初江南多盜，爾忘、爾雪父罕卿董鄉團，捕盜，盜惎焉。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty there were many bandits in Jiangnan; their father Hanqing organized the village militia and captured bandits; the bandits hated them for it.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty there were many bandits in Jiangnan. Their father Hanqing organized the village militia and captured bandits, and the bandits hated them for it.

sentences.zh: 一日自縣還，聞門外呼，罕卿出，為盜縛去。

translations.literal: One day returning from the county seat, he heard someone calling outside the gate; Hanqing went out and was bound and taken away by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: One day, returning from the county seat, he heard someone calling outside the gate. Hanqing went out and was bound and taken away by bandits.

sentences.zh: 爾忘、爾雪方田作，聞馳救，罕卿死橋下矣。

translations.literal: Erwang and Erxue were working in the fields; hearing of it they raced to rescue him, but Hanqing was already dead beneath a bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Erwang and Erxue were working in the fields. Hearing of it, they raced to rescue him, but Hanqing was already dead beneath a bridge.

sentences.zh: 爾忘、爾雪既葬父，仍董鄉團，乃更其初名，「忘」，警忘仇；

translations.literal: After burying their father, Erwang and Erxue still organized the village militia and changed their original names: "Erwang" to warn against forgetting the feud;
translations.idiomatic: After burying their father, Erwang and Erxue continued to organize the village militia and changed their original names: "Erwang," to warn against forgetting the feud;

sentences.zh: 「雪」，冀雪恨也。

translations.literal: "Erxue" in the hope of washing away their hatred.
translations.idiomatic: "Erxue," in the hope of washing away their hatred.

sentences.zh: 每獲盜，必詰執殺罕卿者，久之，知為盜杜息。

translations.literal: Whenever they captured a bandit they questioned him about who had killed Hanqing; after a long time they learned it was the bandit Du Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they captured a bandit, they questioned him about who had killed Hanqing. After a long time they learned it was the bandit Du Xi.

sentences.zh: 息方謀入海，與所左右二人夜治行，爾忘、爾雪诇知之，將壯士奄至息家，縶息及二人者至罕卿死所。

translations.literal: Xi was planning to flee to sea; he and two companions were preparing to travel by night; Erwang and Erxue learned of it through investigation, brought stalwart men and suddenly descended on Xi's house, bound Xi and the two men, and brought them to where Hanqing had died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was planning to flee to sea. He and two companions were preparing to travel by night. Erwang and Erxue learned of it through investigation, brought stalwart men, and suddenly descended on Xi's house. They bound Xi and the two men and brought them to the place where Hanqing had died.

sentences.zh: 比明，爾忘抱罕卿木主至，爾雪於其旁爇釜，爾忘取息舌，爾雪探心肝，且祭且敢，爾忘乃斷息頭。

translations.literal: By dawn Erwang brought Hanqing's spirit tablet; Erxue lit a cauldron beside it; Erwang cut out Xi's tongue, Erxue extracted his heart and liver, making offerings and consuming them as they sacrificed; Erwang then severed Xi's head.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Erwang brought Hanqing's spirit tablet while Erxue lit a cauldron beside it. Erwang cut out Xi's tongue and Erxue extracted his heart and liver, offering sacrifice and consuming the flesh as they did so. Erwang then severed Xi's head.

sentences.zh: 將刃二人者，一讋死，一乞哀，沉諸河。

translations.literal: About to execute the two companions, one died of fright, one begged for mercy and was drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: About to execute the two companions, they found one had died of fright; the other begged for mercy and was drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 爾忘、爾雪持息頭懸罕卿墓，時距罕卿死方踰月。

translations.literal: Erwang and Erxue took Xi's head and hung it at Hanqing's tomb; only just over a month had passed since Hanqing's death.
translations.idiomatic: Erwang and Erxue took Xi's head and hung it at Hanqing's tomb. Only just over a month had passed since Hanqing's death.

sentences.zh: 黃洪元，江南丹陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Hongyuan, a native of Danyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hongyuan was a native of Danyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父國相，與同里虞庠不相能。

translations.literal: His father Guoxiang could not get along with fellow villager Yu Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guoxiang could not get along with a fellow villager named Yu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 方社，國相被酒夜行，庠遣惡少綁而沉諸河。

translations.literal: During a community sacrifice, Guoxiang, drunk, was walking at night; Yu Xiang sent ruffians to bind him and sink him in the river.
translations.idiomatic: During a community sacrifice, Guoxiang, drunk, was walking at night. Yu Xiang sent ruffians to bind him and sink him in the river.

sentences.zh: 洪元與弟福元皆幼，稍長，微聞父死狀，庠欲壻洪元以自解，洪元巽言謝之。

translations.literal: Hongyuan and his younger brother Fuyuan were both young; when they grew somewhat older they faintly heard how their father had died; Yu Xiang wished to marry Hongyuan into his family to settle matters; Hongyuan politely declined with soft words.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan and his younger brother Fuyuan were both young. When they grew older they faintly heard how their father had died. Yu Xiang wished to marry Hongyuan into his family to settle matters, but Hongyuan politely declined with soft words.

sentences.zh: 母喪，既葬，洪元、福元同诇庠所在。

translations.literal: After their mother's funeral and burial, Hongyuan and Fuyuan together tracked down where Yu Xiang was.
translations.idiomatic: After their mother's funeral and burial, Hongyuan and Fuyuan together tracked down Yu Xiang's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 又值社，洪元見庠在社所，還呼福元，各持斧往，洪元入迫庠，字庠曰：「逸群，我死汝！

translations.literal: Again it was time for the community sacrifice; Hongyuan saw Yu Xiang at the sacrificial grounds, went back to call Fuyuan, and each took an axe; Hongyuan entered and pressed close to Yu Xiang, addressed him by his style name: "Yiqun, I die — you die!"
translations.idiomatic: Again it was time for the community sacrifice. Hongyuan saw Yu Xiang at the sacrificial grounds, went back to call Fuyuan, and each took an axe. Hongyuan entered and pressed close to Yu Xiang, addressing him by his style name: "Yiqun, I die — you die!"

sentences.zh: 」庠起猶曰：「孺子醉耶？

translations.literal: Yu Xiang rose and still said: "Has the lad gone drunk?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiang rose and still said, "Has the lad gone drunk?"

sentences.zh: 」洪元曰：「將醉汝血！

translations.literal: Hongyuan said: "I'll drown you in your own blood!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan said, "I'll drown you in your own blood!"

sentences.zh: 」兩斧並舉，遂殺庠。

translations.literal: Both axes rose together and they killed Yu Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Both axes rose together and they killed Yu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詣縣自陳狀，有司義之，免福元，下洪元獄。

translations.literal: They went to the county seat and stated the facts themselves; the officials considered it righteous, released Fuyuan, and imprisoned Hongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They went to the county seat and stated the facts themselves. The officials considered it righteous, released Fuyuan, and imprisoned Hongyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，亦赦出，為浮屠以終。

translations.literal: The next year he too was released by amnesty and became a Buddhist monk for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he too was released by amnesty and became a Buddhist monk for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 顏中和，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Yan Zhonghe, a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhonghe was a native of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 父弘仁。

translations.literal: His father was Hongren.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Hongren.

sentences.zh: 順治初，怨家周昌乘亂誘而殺之，棄其首。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi reign, his enemy Zhou Chang took advantage of the chaos to lure and kill him, and discarded his head.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi reign, his enemy Zhou Chang took advantage of the chaos to lure and kill him, then discarded his head.

sentences.zh: 中和礪斧束藁如人形，書昌姓名以試斧。

translations.literal: Zhonghe sharpened an axe and bound straw into a human shape, writing Zhou Chang's name on it to test the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe sharpened an axe and bound straw into a human shape, writing Zhou Chang's name on it to test the axe.

sentences.zh: 昌聞之，輕中和幼，不為備。

translations.literal: Zhou Chang heard of it but scorned Zhonghe as young and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang heard of it but scorned Zhonghe as too young and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 中和懷斧出跡昌，值市中，尾之行。

translations.literal: Zhonghe hid an axe on his person and went out to track Zhou Chang; encountering him in the market, he followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe hid an axe on his person and went out to track Zhou Chang. Encountering him in the market, he followed behind.

sentences.zh: 稍前，遽揮斧中昌，昌左右顧，又斧之。

translations.literal: Moving slightly ahead, he suddenly swung the axe and struck Zhou Chang; Zhou Chang looked left and right, and he struck again with the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Moving slightly ahead, he suddenly swung the axe and struck Zhou Chang. Zhou Chang looked left and right, and he struck again.

sentences.zh: 母遣其兄孟和走視弟，昌已死。

translations.literal: His mother sent his elder brother Menghe to run and look after his younger brother; Zhou Chang was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: His mother sent his elder brother Menghe to run and look after his younger brother. Zhou Chang was already dead.

sentences.zh: 乃相與詣縣，兄弟爭自承殺人，市人言殺昌者實中和，乃下中和獄。

translations.literal: Then together they went to the county seat; the brothers each insisted on claiming the killing, but market people said it was actually Zhonghe who killed Zhou Chang, so Zhonghe was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Then together they went to the county seat. The brothers each insisted on claiming the killing, but people in the market said it was actually Zhonghe who had killed Zhou Chang, so Zhonghe was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 明年巡按御史錄囚，釋中和。

translations.literal: The next year the touring censor reviewed prisoners and released Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the touring censor reviewed prisoners and released Zhonghe.

sentences.zh: 中和，明義士佩韋從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhonghe was a descendant in the line of the Ming righteous knight Pei Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe was a descendant in the line of the Ming righteous knight Pei Wei.

sentences.zh: 同時又有顏鼇，父仲常，國初為其仇金瑞甫所殺。

translations.literal: At the same time there was also Yan Ao; his father Zhongchang was killed at the founding of the dynasty by his enemy Jin Ruifu.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was also Yan Ao. His father Zhongchang was killed at the founding of the dynasty by his enemy Jin Ruifu.

sentences.zh: 鼇淬刃挾以出入，一日，遇諸胥口，鼇刺瑞甫，入水​​，鼇從之。

translations.literal: Ao kept a sharpened blade and carried it whenever he went out; one day they met at Xukou; Ao stabbed Ruifu, who plunged into the water, and Ao followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ao kept a sharpened blade and carried it whenever he went out. One day they met at Xukou. Ao stabbed Ruifu, who plunged into the water, and Ao followed him in.

sentences.zh: 瑞甫脫去，誣鼇以盜。

translations.literal: Ruifu escaped, and falsely accused Ao of robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Ruifu escaped and falsely accused Ao of robbery.

sentences.zh: 兵備道王紀、同知劉瑞訊得實，為誅瑞甫。

translations.literal: Military intendant Wang Ji and prefectural vice magistrate Liu Rui examined the facts and had Ruifu executed.
translations.idiomatic: Military intendant Wang Ji and prefectural vice magistrate Liu Rui examined the facts and had Ruifu executed.

sentences.zh: 中和復仇時年十六，鼇年十八。

translations.literal: Zhonghe was sixteen when he took revenge; Ao was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe was sixteen when he took revenge; Ao was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 王恩榮，字仁庵，山東蓬萊人。

translations.literal: Wang Enrong, styled Ren'an, a native of Penglai in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Enrong, styled Ren'an, was a native of Penglai in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 縣有小吏寵於官，恩榮父永泰與有隙，被毆死。

translations.literal: In the county there was a petty clerk favored by the officials; Enrong's father Yongtai had a feud with him and was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the county there was a petty clerk favored by the officials. Enrong's father Yongtai had a feud with him and was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 恩榮方九歲，祖母、母皆劉氏。

translations.literal: Enrong was then nine years old; both his grandmother and mother were of the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Enrong was then nine years old. Both his grandmother and mother were of the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 祖母以告官，不得直，畀埋葬銀十兩，內自傷，遽縊。

translations.literal: His grandmother reported it to the authorities but got no justice; they were given ten taels of silver for burial; inwardly grieving, she suddenly hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother reported it to the authorities but got no justice. They were given ten taels of silver for burial. Inwardly grieving, she suddenly hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 母泣血三年，病垂死，以官所畀銀授恩榮曰：「汝家以三喪易此，汝誌之不可忘！

translations.literal: His mother wept blood for three years; when gravely ill and near death she handed Enrong the silver from the authorities and said: "Your family exchanged three deaths for this — you must remember and never forget!"
translations.idiomatic: His mother wept blood for three years. When gravely ill and near death, she handed Enrong the silver from the authorities and said, "Your family exchanged three deaths for this. You must remember and never forget!"

sentences.zh: 恩榮依其舅以居，稍長，補諸生。

translations.literal: Enrong lived with his uncle; when he grew somewhat older he enrolled as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Enrong lived with his uncle. When he grew older he enrolled as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 志復仇，以斧自隨，其舅戒之曰：「汝志固宜爾，然殺人者死，汝父母其餒矣。

translations.literal: Determined to take revenge, he always carried an axe; his uncle warned him: "Your resolve is certainly fitting, yet he who kills is subject to death — your parents would starve."
translations.idiomatic: Determined to take revenge, he always carried an axe. His uncle warned him, "Your resolve is certainly fitting, yet he who kills is subject to death — your parents would starve."

sentences.zh: 」乃娶妻，生子，辭於舅，挾斧行。

translations.literal: So he took a wife, had a son, took leave of his uncle, and set out with his axe.
translations.idiomatic: So he took a wife, had a son, took leave of his uncle, and set out with his axe.

sentences.zh: 遇小吏，揮斧不中，投以石，僕，得救免；

translations.literal: He encountered the petty clerk, swung the axe but missed, threw a stone; the clerk fell and was saved.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the petty clerk, swung the axe but missed, and threw a stone. The clerk fell but was saved.

sentences.zh: 又遇於門，直前斫其首，帽厚，傷未殊。

translations.literal: He encountered him again at a gate, went straight forward and hacked at his head; the hat was thick and the wound was not fatal.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered him again at a gate, went straight forward, and hacked at his head. The hat was thick and the wound was not fatal.

sentences.zh: 訴官，時去永泰死十九年，事無證。

translations.literal: The clerk sued to the authorities; it was then nineteen years since Yongtai's death and there was no evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk sued to the authorities. It was then nineteen years since Yongtai's death, and there was no evidence.

sentences.zh: 恩榮出母所授銀，其上有硃批，旁鈐以血書。

translations.literal: Enrong produced the silver his mother had given him; on it was an official red endorsement, beside which was stamped a blood inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Enrong produced the silver his mother had given him. On it was an official red endorsement, beside which was stamped a blood inscription.

sentences.zh: 知縣歎曰：「孝子也！

translations.literal: The magistrate sighed and said: "A filial son!
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate sighed and said, "A filial son!

sentences.zh: 吾欲聽爾，違國家赦令；

translations.literal: I wish to let you go, but that would violate the state's amnesty decree;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to let you go, but that would violate the state's amnesty decree;

sentences.zh: 吾欲撓爾，傷人子至情。

translations.literal: I wish to obstruct you, but that would wound a son's utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to obstruct you, but that would wound a son's utmost feeling.

sentences.zh: 周官有調人，其各相避已耳。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou provides for mediators — let each avoid the other, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou provides for mediators — let each avoid the other, that is all.

sentences.zh: 」於是恩榮哭，堂上下皆哭，小吏避之棲霞。

translations.literal: Then Enrong wept, and all above and below in the hall wept; the petty clerk fled to Qixia to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Then Enrong wept, and all above and below in the hall wept. The petty clerk fled to Qixia to hide.

sentences.zh: 居八年，一日，方入城，過小巷，恩榮與遇，小吏無所逃，乞貸死。

translations.literal: After eight years, one day as he was entering the city and passing through a narrow lane, Enrong encountered him; the petty clerk had nowhere to flee and begged to be spared his life.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years, one day as he was entering the city and passing through a narrow lane, Enrong encountered him. The petty clerk had nowhere to flee and begged to be spared his life.

sentences.zh: 恩榮曰：「吾父遲爾久矣！

translations.literal: Enrong said: "My father has waited long for you!"
translations.idiomatic: Enrong said, "My father has waited long for you!"

sentences.zh: 」斧裂其腦，以足蹴其心，死。

translations.literal: With his axe he split the clerk's skull and kicked his heart with his foot — dead.
translations.idiomatic: With his axe he split the clerk's skull and kicked his heart with his foot. He was dead.

sentences.zh: 乃詣縣，小吏家言永泰故自縊，非毆死，當發棺以驗。

translations.literal: Then he went to the county seat; the petty clerk's family said Yongtai had originally hanged himself, not been beaten to death, and that the coffin should be opened for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went to the county seat. The petty clerk's family said Yongtai had originally hanged himself rather than been beaten to death, and that the coffin should be opened for verification.

sentences.zh: 恩榮曰：「民原抵罪死，不原暴父骸。

translations.literal: Enrong said: "I am willing to accept punishment and die, but I will not allow my father's remains to be violated."
translations.idiomatic: Enrong said, "I am willing to accept punishment and die, but I will not allow my father's remains to be violated."

sentences.zh: 」叩頭流血。

translations.literal: He knocked his head on the ground until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: He knocked his head on the ground until it bled.

sentences.zh: 知縣諮於眾，皆曰：「恩榮言是。

translations.literal: The magistrate consulted the crowd; all said: "Enrong speaks correctly."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate consulted the crowd. All said, "Enrong speaks correctly."

sentences.zh: 」具狀上按察使，按察使議曰：「律不言復仇，然擅殺行凶人，罪止杖六十，即時殺死者不論，是未嘗不許人復仇也。

translations.literal: He submitted a report to the provincial surveillance commissioner, who deliberated: "The law does not speak of revenge, yet unauthorized killing of an assailant carries a penalty of only sixty blows; killing on the spot is not prosecuted — thus revenge has never been wholly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a report to the provincial surveillance commissioner, who deliberated, "The law does not speak of revenge, yet unauthorized killing of an assailant carries a penalty of only sixty blows, and killing on the spot is not prosecuted — thus revenge has never been wholly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 恩榮父死時未成童，其後屢復仇不遂，非即時，猶即時矣。

translations.literal: When Enrong's father died he was not yet of age; afterward he repeatedly attempted revenge without success — though not immediate, it is as good as immediate.
translations.idiomatic: When Enrong's father died he was not yet of age. Afterward he repeatedly attempted revenge without success — though not immediate, it is as good as immediate.

sentences.zh: 況其視死無畏，剛烈有足嘉者，當特予開釋，復其諸生。

translations.literal: Moreover, his fearlessness before death and fierce integrity are truly admirable; he should be specially released and restored to his status as licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his fearlessness before death and fierce integrity are truly admirable. He should be specially released and restored to his status as licentiate.

sentences.zh: 」有司將請旌，其舅為辭罷。

translations.literal: The authorities were about to request an imperial commendation, but his uncle declined on his behalf and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were about to request an imperial commendation, but his uncle declined on his behalf and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 楊獻恆，山東益都人。

translations.literal: Yang Xianheng, a native of Yidu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xianheng was a native of Yidu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父加官，與濟南楊開泰有隙，詈其門，開泰訟焉。

translations.literal: His father Jiaguan had a feud with Yang Kaitai of Jinan; he cursed at Kaitai's gate, and Kaitai sued him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiaguan had a feud with Yang Kaitai of Jinan. He cursed at Kaitai's gate, and Kaitai sued him.

sentences.zh: 加官率獻恆走求援，開泰遣其徒紿使出小徑，要而毆之，加官死焉。

translations.literal: Jiaguan took Xianheng and fled to seek help; Kaitai sent his followers to lure them out by a small path, intercepted and beat them, and Jiaguan died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaguan took Xianheng and fled to seek help. Kaitai sent his followers to lure them out by a small path, intercepted and beat them, and Jiaguan died.

sentences.zh: 獻恆死復甦，開泰以他事誣之，下濟南獄。

translations.literal: Xianheng died and revived; Kaitai framed him on another charge and he was sent to prison in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianheng died and revived. Kaitai framed him on another charge and he was sent to prison in Jinan.

sentences.zh: 山東初設總督，獻恆訟焉，下青州府勘問，直獻恆，開泰以賄免。

translations.literal: When Shandong first established a governor-general, Xianheng sued there; the case was sent down to Qingzhou Prefecture for investigation, which found in Xianheng's favor, but Kaitai escaped through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong first established a governor-general, Xianheng sued there. The case was sent down to Qingzhou Prefecture for investigation, which found in Xianheng's favor, but Kaitai escaped through bribery.

sentences.zh: 獻恆走京師叩閽，下山東巡撫會鞫，罰開泰納埋葬銀四十兩，迫獻恆具領。

translations.literal: Xianheng went to the capital and petitioned at the palace gate; the case was sent down to the Shandong governor, who jointly tried it and fined Kaitai forty taels of burial silver, forcing Xianheng to sign a receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Xianheng went to the capital and petitioned at the palace gate. The case was sent down to the Shandong governor, who jointly tried it, fined Kaitai forty taels of burial silver, and forced Xianheng to sign a receipt.

sentences.zh: 獻恆藏銀典肆，再走京師叩閽，下山東巡撫，以獄已定罪，獻恆妄訴，笞四十。

translations.literal: Xianheng deposited the silver in a pawnshop and again went to the capital to petition; the case was sent down to the Shandong governor, who ruled that since the case had already been decided, Xianheng's complaint was groundless, and had him beaten forty blows.
translations.idiomatic: Xianheng deposited the silver in a pawnshop and again went to the capital to petition. The case was sent down to the Shandong governor, who ruled that since the case had already been decided, Xianheng's complaint was groundless, and had him beaten forty blows.

sentences.zh: 開泰計必欲殺獻恆，遣其子承恩至青州謀諸吏。

translations.literal: Kaitai resolved that he must kill Xianheng and sent his son Chengen to Qingzhou to conspire with the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai resolved that he must kill Xianheng and sent his son Chengen to Qingzhou to conspire with the clerks.

sentences.zh: 獻恆潛知之，持鐵骨朵挾刃至所居。

translations.literal: Xianheng secretly learned of it, took an iron mace and a blade, and went to where Chengen was staying.
translations.idiomatic: Xianheng secretly learned of it, took an iron mace and a blade, and went to where Chengen was staying.

sentences.zh: 承恩方與吏耳語，伺其出，以鐵骨朵擊之，僕，急拔刀斷其喉，又抉其睛噉之，詣縣自陳，出所藏銀為證。

translations.literal: Chengen was whispering with a clerk; when he came out, Xianheng struck him with the iron mace and he fell; he quickly drew his knife and cut Chengen's throat, gouged out his eyes and ate them, then went to the county seat to state the facts himself, producing the deposited silver as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen was whispering with a clerk. When he came out, Xianheng struck him with the iron mace and he fell. Xianheng quickly drew his knife, cut Chengen's throat, gouged out his eyes and ate them, then went to the county seat to state the facts himself, producing the deposited silver as evidence.

sentences.zh: 縣具獄，得末減，遣戍。

translations.literal: The county prepared the case; he received a reduced sentence and was sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: The county prepared the case. He received a reduced sentence and was sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 任騎馬，直隸新城人。

translations.literal: Ren Qima, a native of Xincheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Qima was a native of Xincheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父為仇所戕，死以四月八日，方賽神，被二十八創。

translations.literal: His father had been killed by an enemy; he died on the eighth day of the fourth month during a village sacrifice, suffering twenty-eight wounds.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been killed by an enemy. He died on the eighth day of the fourth month during a village sacrifice, suffering twenty-eight wounds.

sentences.zh: 騎馬時方幼，至七歲，問母，得父死狀，慟憤，以爪刺胸，血出。

translations.literal: Qima was then very young; at seven he asked his mother and learned how his father had died; grief and rage overwhelmed him and he scratched his chest with his fingernails until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: Qima was then very young. At seven he asked his mother and learned how his father had died. Grief and rage overwhelmed him and he scratched his chest with his fingernails until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 悲至，輒如是，以為常。

translations.literal: Whenever grief overcame him he did the same — it became his habit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever grief overcame him he did the same — it became his habit.

sentences.zh: 其仇姓馬，因自名騎馬。

translations.literal: His enemy's surname was Ma, so he named himself Qima.
translations.idiomatic: His enemy's surname was Ma, so he named himself Qima.

sentences.zh: 長，慮仇且疑，乃字伯超，詭自況馬超也。

translations.literal: When he grew up, fearing the enemy might grow suspicious, he styled himself Bochao, pretending to compare himself to Ma Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, fearing the enemy might grow suspicious, he styled himself Bochao, pretending to compare himself to Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 母欲與議婚，力拒。

translations.literal: When his mother wished to arrange a marriage for him, he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother wished to arrange a marriage for him, he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 母死，治葬，且營祭田。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he arranged her burial and also set aside sacrificial fields.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he arranged her burial and also set aside sacrificial fields.

sentences.zh: 年十九，四月八日復賽神，騎馬度仇必至，懷刃待於路。

translations.literal: At nineteen, on the eighth day of the fourth month when the village sacrifice was held again, Qima judged the enemy would surely come and waited on the road with a blade hidden on his person.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, on the eighth day of the fourth month when the village sacrifice was held again, Qima judged the enemy would surely come and waited on the road with a blade hidden on his person.

sentences.zh: 仇至，與漫語，指其笠問值，騎馬左手脫笠授仇，蔽其目，右手出刃急刺，洞仇胸，亦二十八創乃止。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived, they chatted idly; Qima pointed at his hat and asked its price; with his left hand he removed the hat and handed it to the enemy, blocking his eyes, and with his right drew his blade and stabbed swiftly, piercing the enemy's chest — he stopped only after twenty-eight wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived, they chatted idly. Qima pointed at his hat and asked its price. With his left hand he removed the hat and handed it to the enemy, blocking his eyes, and with his right drew his blade and stabbed swiftly, piercing the enemy's chest. He stopped only after inflicting twenty-eight wounds.

sentences.zh: 仇妻子至，怖甚，騎馬曰：「吾殺父仇，於汝母子何與？

translations.literal: The enemy's wife and children arrived, terrified; Qima said: "I killed my father's enemy — what has that to do with you, mother and son?"
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's wife and children arrived, terrified. Qima said, "I killed my father's enemy — what has that to do with you, mother and son?"

sentences.zh: 」乃詣縣自首。

translations.literal: Then he went to the county seat and surrendered himself.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went to the county seat and surrendered himself.

sentences.zh: 知縣欲生之，曰：「彼殺汝，汝奪刃殺之耶？

translations.literal: The magistrate wished to spare his life and said: "When he killed you, did you seize his blade and kill him?"
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate wished to spare his life and said, "When he killed you, did you seize his blade and kill him?"

sentences.zh: 」騎馬對曰：「民痛父十餘年，乃今得報之，若幸脫死，謂彼非吾仇，民不原也。

translations.literal: Qima replied: "Your subject has grieved for his father more than ten years and has now at last taken revenge. If I should luckily escape death, and people say he was not my enemy, I would not accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Qima replied, "Your subject has grieved for his father more than ten years and has now at last taken revenge. If I should luckily escape death and people say he was not my enemy, I would not accept it."

sentences.zh: 」因袒，出爪痕殷然，見者皆流涕。

translations.literal: He bared his chest, revealing the claw marks still vivid; all who saw wept.
translations.idiomatic: He bared his chest, revealing the claw marks still vivid. All who saw wept.

sentences.zh: 獄具，得緩決。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, he received a deferred sentence.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete, he received a deferred sentence.

sentences.zh: 在獄十餘年，知縣嘗使出祭墓，辭，怪而問之，曰：「仇亦有子，假使效我而斫我。

translations.literal: Imprisoned for more than ten years, the magistrate once sent him out to tend his family graves; he declined. Asked in surprise, he said: "The enemy also has a son. Suppose he imitated me and hacked me down."
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned for more than ten years, the magistrate once sent him out to tend his family graves, but he declined. Asked in surprise, he said, "The enemy also has a son. Suppose he imitated me and hacked me down."

sentences.zh: 我死，分也，奈何以累公？

translations.literal: "If I die, that is my portion — but how could I burden Your Honor?"
translations.idiomatic: "If I die, that is my portion — but how could I burden Your Honor?"

sentences.zh: 」新城人皆賢之，請於縣，築室獄傍，為娶妻生子。

translations.literal: The people of Xincheng all considered him worthy; they petitioned the county to build a house beside the prison, found him a wife, and he had a son.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xincheng all considered him worthy. They petitioned the county to build a house beside the prison, found him a wife, and he had a son.

sentences.zh: 久之，赦出。

translations.literal: After a long time he was released by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was released by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 知縣後至者欲見之，輒辭。

translations.literal: Later magistrates who arrived wished to see him, but he always declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later magistrates who arrived wished to see him, but he always declined.

sentences.zh: 聞其習形家言，以相宅召，又謝不往，曰：「官宅不同於民，若言不利，且興役，是以吾言擾民也。

translations.literal: Hearing that he studied geomancy, one summoned him to inspect an official residence; again he declined, saying: "An official residence is not the same as a commoner's home. If I said it was unfavorable and labor were raised, my words would disturb the people."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that he studied geomancy, one summoned him to inspect an official residence. Again he declined, saying, "An official residence is not the same as a commoner's home. If I said it was unfavorable and labor were raised, my words would disturb the people."

sentences.zh: 」既卒，總督曾國籓旌其廬曰「孝義剛烈」。

translations.literal: After he died, Governor-General Zeng Guofan commended his dwelling with the inscription "Filial, Righteous, and Fiercely Upright."
translations.idiomatic: After he died, Governor-General Zeng Guofan commended his dwelling with the inscription "Filial, Righteous, and Fiercely Upright."

sentences.zh: 李巨勳，甘肅禮縣人。

translations.literal: Li Juxun, a native of Li County in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Juxun was a native of Li County in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 回亂，土豪羅五殺其父，巨勳欲赴死，母以弟幼沮之，命之娶，不可，乃訟五，五繫獄，始娶生子。

translations.literal: During the Muslim rebellion, local strongman Luo Wu killed his father. Juxun wished to go and die in revenge, but his mother, because his younger brother was still small, dissuaded him and ordered him to marry; he refused. Only after he sued Wu and Wu was imprisoned did he marry and have a son.
translations.idiomatic: During the Muslim rebellion, the local strongman Luo Wu killed his father. Juxun wished to go and die in revenge, but his mother, because his younger brother was still small, dissuaded him and ordered him to marry. He refused. Only after he sued Wu and Wu was imprisoned did he marry and have a son.

sentences.zh: 五以賄出獄，巨勳與弟恆挾刃伺五。

translations.literal: Wu bribed his way out of prison; Juxun and his younger brother constantly carried blades and watched for Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu bribed his way out of prison. Juxun and his younger brother constantly carried blades and watched for Wu.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，竟擊殺五，巨勳自首繫獄，瘐死。

translations.literal: In the early Guangxu reign he finally struck and killed Wu. Juxun surrendered himself and was imprisoned, where he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu reign he finally struck and killed Wu. Juxun surrendered himself and was imprisoned, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 母不食，亦卒。

translations.literal: His mother stopped eating and also died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother stopped eating and also died.

sentences.zh: 妻張，撫孤子成立。

translations.literal: His wife Zhang raised their orphaned son to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Zhang raised their orphaned son to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 任四，甘肅渭源人，農也。

translations.literal: Ren Si, a native of Weiyuan in Gansu, was a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Si was a native of Weiyuan in Gansu and was a farmer.

sentences.zh: 徙家狄道，父死於虎，四乃習鳥槍，誓殺百虎報父仇。

translations.literal: He moved his family to Didao; his father died at the hands of a tiger. Si then learned to use a bird gun and swore to kill a hundred tigers to avenge his father.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his family to Didao. His father died at the hands of a tiger. Si then learned to use a bird gun and swore to kill a hundred tigers to avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 遇虎，槍一發立殕。

translations.literal: When he encountered a tiger, one shot from his gun brought it down instantly.
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered a tiger, one shot from his gun brought it down instantly.

sentences.zh: 鄰縣有虎，輒迎四往捕，必得。

translations.literal: When neighboring counties had tigers, they always invited Si to come and hunt them, and he always succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When neighboring counties had tigers, they always invited Si to come and hunt them, and he always succeeded.

sentences.zh: 四已老，計所殺虎九十有九，復入山伺虎，虎驟至，槍不及發，幾為所噬。

translations.literal: Si was already old; he calculated he had killed ninety-nine tigers. He entered the mountains again to wait for a tiger; a tiger suddenly appeared and he had no time to fire — he was nearly devoured.
translations.idiomatic: Si was already old. He calculated he had killed ninety-nine tigers and entered the mountains again to wait. A tiger suddenly appeared and he had no time to fire — he was nearly devoured.

sentences.zh: 俄雲起晝晦，虎自去，四歸祭父，戒子孫毋更仇虎，遂以無疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon clouds rose and daylight darkened; the tiger left on its own. Si returned to sacrifice to his father, admonished his descendants never again to feud with tigers, and died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon clouds rose and daylight darkened. The tiger left on its own. Si returned to sacrifice to his father, admonished his descendants never again to feud with tigers, and died without illness.

sentences.zh: 卒時，猶寢虎皮也。

translations.literal: When he died, he was still sleeping on a tiger skin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was still sleeping on a tiger skin.

sentences.zh: =王國林=王國林，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Wang Guolin, a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guolin was a native of Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 有膂力。

translations.literal: He had great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: He had great physical strength.

sentences.zh: 虎咥其父，國林奮擊，折虎左牙。

translations.literal: A tiger seized his father in its jaws; Guolin fought fiercely and broke the tiger's left fang.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger seized his father in its jaws. Guolin fought fiercely and broke the tiger's left fang.

sentences.zh: 虎怒，爪其腹，腹破，腸出尺許，而父卒死。

translations.literal: The tiger in rage clawed his belly; his belly tore open and intestines spilled out more than a foot, yet his father still died.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger in rage clawed his belly. His belly tore open and intestines spilled out more than a foot, yet his father still died.

sentences.zh: 國林死复甦，家人納其腸，為縫腹，得愈。

translations.literal: Guolin died and revived; his family pushed his intestines back in, sewed up his belly, and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin died and revived. His family pushed his intestines back in, sewed up his belly, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 乃制火器獵虎，最後獲一虎，左牙折，知為咥父者，烹之，告父墓。

translations.literal: He then made a firearm to hunt tigers. At last he caught a tiger with a broken left fang and knew it was the one that had seized his father; he cooked it and reported to his father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He then made a firearm to hunt tigers. At last he caught a tiger with a broken left fang and knew it was the one that had seized his father. He cooked it and reported to his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 藍忠，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lan Zhong, a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Zhong was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 家萬山中，父元章，與叔裕比屋居。

translations.literal: His family lived deep in the mountains; his father Yuanzhang and his uncle Yu lived in neighboring houses.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived deep in the mountains. His father Yuanzhang and his uncle Yu lived in neighboring houses.

sentences.zh: 有虎夜出，中伏弩，跳踉入所居村。

translations.literal: A tiger came out at night, struck by a hidden crossbow; it leaped and stumbled into the village where they lived.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger came out at night, struck by a hidden crossbow. It leaped and stumbled into the village where they lived.

sentences.zh: 裕夢中聞虎至，呼，虎撲門不得入，登屋毀杗桷直下，齧殺裕。

translations.literal: Yu, in a dream, heard the tiger arrive and cried out; the tiger pounced at the door but could not enter, climbed the roof, broke through the rafters and descended, and bit Yu to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, in a dream, heard the tiger arrive and cried out. The tiger pounced at the door but could not enter, climbed the roof, broke through the rafters and descended, and bit Yu to death.

sentences.zh: 元章聞裕為虎殺，复呼，虎循聲至，破屋撲元章，僕。

translations.literal: Yuanzhang heard that Yu had been killed by a tiger and cried out again; the tiger followed the sound, broke through the house, and pounced on Yuanzhang, who fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhang heard that Yu had been killed by a tiger and cried out again. The tiger followed the sound, broke through the house, and pounced on Yuanzhang, who fell.

sentences.zh: 忠持長刀直前，刺虎中喉，刃入腹三尺許。

translations.literal: Zhong took a long knife and went straight forward, stabbing the tiger in the throat; the blade entered more than three feet into its belly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong took a long knife and went straight forward, stabbing the tiger in the throat. The blade entered more than three feet into its belly.

sentences.zh: 虎舍元章撲忠，忠拔刀柄脫，妻卓搤虎頸，連呼曰：「斧！

translations.literal: The tiger released Yuanzhang and pounced on Zhong; Zhong pulled but the knife handle came free. His wife Zhuo seized the tiger's neck and cried repeatedly: "Axe!"
translations.idiomatic: The tiger released Yuanzhang and pounced on Zhong. Zhong pulled but the knife handle came free. His wife Zhuo seized the tiger's neck and cried repeatedly, "Axe!"

sentences.zh: 」忠自門後取斧力斫之。

translations.literal: Zhong took an axe from behind the door and hacked at it with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong took an axe from behind the door and hacked at it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 天明：力且盡，視虎已殪。

translations.literal: At dawn his strength was nearly spent; he looked and saw the tiger was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn his strength was nearly spent. He looked and saw the tiger was already dead.

sentences.zh: 元章尚臥地，忠與妻扶就寢，越日，創甚竟死。

translations.literal: Yuanzhang still lay on the ground; Zhong and his wife helped him to bed, but after a day his wounds were severe and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhang still lay on the ground. Zhong and his wife helped him to bed, but after a day his wounds were severe and he died.
